                                                                                              Agriculture: key facts from the book
                                                                                              • Agriculture plays a vital role in India's economy. 54.6% of the total workforce is engaged in agriculture and allied sector activity (Census 2011) and accounts for 18.4% of India's GVA at current prices during 2022-23.

                                                                                              As per the Provisional Estimates of National Income, 2023- 24 released by National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistic & Programme Implementation, the agriculture and allied sector contributed approximately 17.7% of India's Gross Value Added (GVA) at current prices during 2023-24.

                                                                                              • First Agricultural University of the country was established in 1960. Inauguration of this University (Uttar Pradesh Agricultural University) was done by Jawaharlal Nehru on 17 November 1960 in Pantnagar. Later, it was named as Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology.

                                                                                              • 'History of Indian Agriculture' is written by M.S. Randhawa (Mohinder Singh Randhawa). According to standards of Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), for secure storage of food grains, relative humidity should be kept at 14%.
                                                                                              • Double cropping means when two or more than two crops are grown in one crop year at one place. Intercropping is the practice of growing two or more crops in proximity.
                                                                                              • Mixed farming refers to growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock. By practicing this, farmers can increase their income.
                                                                                              • Punjab is leading state in implementing ‘Contract farming’. Sikkim is a hilly state in North-East. Its maximum area is covered under forest. Less than 10% of total land is available for agriculture in this state. On the contrary, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana are the major food grain-producing states. According to Agricultural Statistics at a Glance 2024- 25, the state of Uttar Pradesh has the largest share (17.85%) in the total food grain production (2024-25) in India. As per the latest data 2022-23 (P) of the Ministry of Agriculture of India, Net Area Sown in India is 45.88%, Forest area is

                                                                                              23.49% and land under other practices is 30.63%. Among the top 10 rice producing countries in the world, India is the first and China is at the second place (FAO, 2024). About

                                                                                              37.27% of the gross area of food grain in India (2024-25) is under rice cultivation.

                                                                                              • On the basis of the data of the year 2024-25, the largest Fertilizers in terms of Nutrients (N.P.&K) consumption in terms of thousand tonnes in five states respectively Uttar Pradesh (5563.82 thousand tonnes), Maharashtra (3274.17 thousand tonnes), Madhya Pradesh (3203.31 thousand tonnes), Karnataka (2325.04 thousand tonnes) and Punjab (2042.09 thousand tonnes).
                                                                                              • Balanced fertilizers are used to increase production, to improve the quality of food grains and to maintain land productivity.
                                                                                              • Seed village concept is a concept based on a village where a trained group of farmers are involved in production of seeds of various crops and cater to the needs of themselves and fellow farmers of the villages and farmers of the neighbouring villages in appropriate timely manner and at an affordable cost.
                                                                                              • Agmark is a quality certification mark granted by the government of India under Agricultural produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937. Various steps have been taken by the Government of India for the continuous development of agriculture.
                                                                                              • To increase farmers in come, the Government has promoted sustainable soil fertility through the Soil Health Card Scheme; expanded assured irrigation, improved on farm water-use efficiency and enhanced physical access to water through the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY); supported organic farming through the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY); and taken steps to create an Integrated National Agriculture Market through e-NAM (National Agriculture Market).
                                                                                              • Kisan Credit Card (K.C.C.) scheme is implemented across the country through commercial banks, small finance banks, co-operative banks and regional-rural banks.

                                                                                              Green Manure: Prior to the sowing of the crop seeds, some plants like sun hemp or guar are grown and then mulched by ploughing them into the soil. These green plants thus turn into green manure which helps in enriching the soil in nitrogen and phosphorus.

A farm gets 84-105 kg/hectare nitrogen from Dhaincha, 68-85 kg/hectare from Guar and 74-88 kg/ hectare from Lobia.

                                                                                                    Green Revolution: key facts from the book
                                                                                                    • Norman Ernest Borlaug is the father of Green Revolution in the world. He was born on 25th March 1914 in Iowa State of America.

                                                                                                    Wheat production has been doubled in India-Pakistan and Mexico due to a high yielding variety of seeds developed by him. Borlaug is among those seven persons in the world who got all the three awards viz. Nobel Peace Prize, 'Presidential Medal of Freedom' and Congressional Gold Medal.

                                                                                                    • Borlaug has been honoured with Padma-Vibhushan of India in 2006.
                                                                                                    • Dr. M.S. Swaminathan is widely regarded as the Father of the Green Revolution in India. Under his leadership (in collaboration with Norman Borlaug), semi dwarf high-yielding wheat varieties developed in Mexico were introduced in India and then tested adapted and multiplied for India condition, lealding to the spread of HYV seeds in India. Apart from this, special emphasis was given on the increased use of fertilizers and adequate development of irrigation facilities. In India, the programme to promote high yielding (developed) seeds was started by the Government of India with support from several international organisation and foundation, including the Rockefeller foundation.
                                                                                                    • First stage of Green Revolution was carried out in India from 1960s to 1970s. Its second stage was implemented in the period of 1980s. Its third stage was started in the year 1995 and covered almost all the areas of the country.
                                                                                                    • The most benefitted crop in production and productivity by the green revolution in India is wheat.

                                                                                                    Before Green Revolution, the production of wheat all over India was 12.26 Million tonnes whereas in 2000-2001 it became 69.68 million tons and in 2024-25 is 117.94 million tons.

                                                                                                    • The increase occurred due to the increase in yield per Hectare. After wheat, the highest impact of the Green Revolution was seen on rice cultivation.
                                                                                                    • The main plant in the Green Revolution was the wheat of Mexican species which was brought from Borlaug’s International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT).
                                                                                                    • In the year, 2023-24 the production of wheat reached up to 3559 kg/Hectare.
                                                                                                    • High yielding variety of seeds, fertilizer, irrigation, use of technology, marketing, and industrialization of agriculture is known as Green Revolution.

                                                                                                    On 28 July 2000, the Central Government announced a new National Agriculture Policy. Under this policy the concept of rainbow revolution was proposed. In this policy, all the revolutions directly or indirectly related to agricultural activities were included.

                                                                                                    Various Revolutions and its Areas

                                                                                                    Green Revolution Food production or crop production

                                                                                                    Golden Revolution

                                                                                                    Fruit and Vegetable production

                                                                                                    White RevolutionMilk Production
                                                                                                    Brown RevolutionFertilizer Production / Non

                                                                                                    conventional Energy

                                                                                                    Blue RevolutionFish Production
                                                                                                    Red RevolutionMeat/Tomato Production
                                                                                                    Black RevolutionPetroleum Production

                                                                                                    Round Revolution

                                                                                                    Potato Production

                                                                                                    Yellow RevolutionOilseed Production
                                                                                                    Pink RevolutionOnion Production/Export of Meat

                                                                                                    'National Zero till seed cum fertilizer drill' developed by G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology. This machine enables to sow directly after paddy harvest without prior seed-bed preparation.

                                                                                                    Food Crops: key facts from the book

                                                                                                    i. Rabi Crops

                                                                                                    • In India, due to ecological differences in various regions different types of cropping pattern are adopted. For example, rice and wheat in Punjab, Haryana, West U.P. etc. There are three different crop seasons in India –

                                                                                                    Rabi Crops

                                                                                                    Kharif Crops

                                                                                                    Zaid Crops

                                                                                                    • Rabi Crops are sown in winter between October and November and harvested in summer between March and April. Major Rabi crops are - Wheat, Mustard, Potato, Gram, Pea, Lentil, Barley etc. In winter, rainfalls due to temperate western disturbances help in the production of these crops.
                                                                                                    • Wheat is the second most important cereal crop of India. It is produced in north and north-western regions. For the cultivation of wheat, the temperature should be between 10°C-25°C and an average annual rainfall of 50 to 75 cm evenly distributed over the growing season is required.
                                                                                                    • According to Economic Survey data 2024-25, the cultivation of wheat in India is done on 31.8 Million Hectare (2023-24). Some important varieties of wheat are - Sonalika, Arjun, Kundan, Amar (HW-2004), Bhawani (HW-1085), Chandrika (HPW-184), Deshratna (BR-104), Kanchan (DL-803), Gomti (K-9465) etc. For the enhancement in production of wheat in India, dwarf species has been developed for wheat by agricultural scientists. In which Lerma Rojo 64-A, Sonora-63, Sonora-64, Mayo 64 and S-227 have been examined in wheat productive states of the Country.
                                                                                                    • Due to the successful tests of dwarf wheat varieties, the production of wheat has been increased. Norin-10 is a gene of dwarfism in Wheat. Macaroni wheat is suitable for cultivation in dry condition or unirrigated area. Kalyan Sona (Kalyan Gold) is an advanced type of wheat varieties.
                                                                                                    • Yellow rust, Brown rust and Black rust are three types of rust diseases found in wheat.
                                                                                                    • Karnal Bunt is a fungal disease of wheat. This is caused by the smut fungus Tilletia indica Mitra. The disease was first recognized in the year 1931.
                                                                                                    • Tirtikale is a hybrid of wheat and rye.
                                                                                                    • According to 2024-25 data, Uttar Pradesh (35.65 million tonnes) is the largest producer of wheat. Madhya Pradesh (24.51 million tonnes) and Punjab (17.99 million tonnes) are placed at second and third position respectively.
                                                                                                    • Green Revolution was the result of adaptation of the new Agricultural Strategy, which was introduced in the 20th century during decades of –Seventies

                                                                                                    Green Revolution (New Agricultural Strategy) → began 1966-67; first stage covered Haryana, Punjab and western Uttar Pradesh.

                                                                                                          Food Crops · Kharif Crops: key facts from the book
                                                                                                          • Kharif Crops are sown with the initiation of Monsoon in different regions and harvested in October-November. Major Kharif crops are - Paddy, Millet, Soybean, Peanut, etc. Soybean is also a Kharif crop. Paddy is grown mainly in Assam, West Bengal, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Konkan coast area of Maharashtra, U.P. and Bihar. Development of irrigation system led to its cultivation in Punjab and Haryana also.
                                                                                                          • Paddy is a tropical crop. For the cultivation of Rice, the required normal temperature is above 25°C and average annual rainfall more than 100 cm. Rice is one of the important food crops in India. According to data Agricultural Statistics at a Glance 2024-25, in the year 2024-25, 51.27 million hectares area of India is covered under rice cultivation.
                                                                                                          • According to data Agricultural Statistics at a Glance, 2024- 25 in the year 2024-25 the largest area under rice cultivation is in Uttar Pradesh (7.35 million hectares). West Bengal (5.59 million hectares) stands in second place and Telangana (4.81 million hectares) in the third place.
                                                                                                          • Highest rice productivity in India is in Punjab. Productivity in Punjab was 4428 kg per hectare in 2024-25. The average rice productivity per hectare in India is 2929 kg per hectare in 2024-25.
                                                                                                          • The deltaic region of Krishna and Godavari is known as 'Rice Bowl of India'. The region falls under the state of Andhra Pradesh.

                                                                                                          Major rice producing region are Telangana and Rayal seema which is extended on the Krishan-Godavari delta.

                                                                                                          • According to data Agricultural Statistics at a Glance 2024- 25, the leading rice-producing states in 2024-25 are –

                                                                                                          (1) Uttar Pradesh (20.76 Million Tonnes)

                                                                                                          (2) Telangana (17.45 Million Tonnes)

                                                                                                          (3) West Bengal (16.02 Million Tonnes)

                                                                                                          • Main varieties of Paddy in India are Jamuna, Cauvery, Jaya, Kanchi, Jagannath, Krishna, Hansa, Vijaya, Padma, Annapurna, Bala and Ratna. Aman rice is sown in June-July and harvested in November-December.
                                                                                                          • Pusa-Sugandh is an aromatic variety of rice. Pusa RH-10 is a hybrid Basmati rice. Other hybrid varieties are PHB 71, Ganga, Suruchi-5401, KRH-2, Sahyadri-4.
                                                                                                          • The proper seed rate for transplanting of Basmati rice is 15-20 kg per hectare.
                                                                                                          • Barani Deep, Narendra Shankar Dhan, Narendra Shuska Samrat, Lalmati etc. are varieties of Rice.
                                                                                                          • Blue Green Algae, Azospirillum, Phosphobacteria and Azolla are important Bio-fertilizers.
                                                                                                          Cash Crops: key facts from the book

                                                                                                          i. Cotton:

                                                                                                          • Cotton is the one of the most important commercial crop of India. It is raw material for cotton textile industry. Cotton belongs to the Malvaceae Family. There are two major varieties of cotton found in the world. (i) Old world cotton

                                                                                                          (ii) New world cotton

                                                                                                          • Cotton is an indigenous plant of India. It is also mentioned in the ancient text such as Rigveda and Manusmriti. India is the first country in the world where hybrid cotton has been developed resulting in enhanced production.
                                                                                                          • Black soil is most suitable for its cultivation. The temperature ranging between 25°C-35°C, 210 Frost Free day, clear sky, bright sunshine and annual rainfall of 75-100 cms are favourable conditions for its cultivation.
                                                                                                          • North-Western and western India are major producing regions of cotton.
                                                                                                          • According to data from the Economic Survey 2025-26, the three leading states in cotton production are (in 2024-25)-

                                                                                                          1. Maharashtra 7.37 Million Bales (170 kg. of each).

                                                                                                          2. Gujarat 7.16 Million Bales (170 kg. of each).

                                                                                                          3. Telangana 5.79 Million Bales (170 kg. of each).

                                                                                                          • Maharashtra is largely covered under black soil which is most suitable soil for cotton cultivation. Cotton is known as White gold in Maharashtra.
                                                                                                          • Cotton cultivation in Madhya Pradesh is done on the western side of the state e.g. Plateau of Malwa and Narmada Valley. The main cotton producing district are East and West Nimar, Dhar, Dewas, Shajapur, Ujjain, Ratlam, Khandwa, Hoshangabad and Rajgarh.
                                                                                                          • Khandwa - Khargone region is also known as ‘white gold’ region due to the cultivation of cotton.
                                                                                                          • Cotton Fibers are collected from cotton seeds.
                                                                                                          • Rice originated in –South-East Asia

                                                                                                          Rice → originated in South-East Asia; needs temperature above 25°C and rainfall above 100 cm.

                                                                                                                Cash Crops · Sugarcane: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                • It is a tropical as well as a sub-tropical crop. It grows well in a hot and humid climate with the temperature ranging between 21°C to 27°C and an annual rainfall between 75 cm and 100 cm. Irrigation is required in the regions of low rainfall.
                                                                                                                • According to the data of the year 2024-25 three leading states in Sugarcane production are -

                                                                                                                1. Uttar Pradesh (220.80 Million tonnes).

                                                                                                                2. Maharashtra (109.97 Million Tonnes)

                                                                                                                3. Karnataka (48.06 Million tonnes)

                                                                                                                The sustainable sugarcane initiative (SSI) is an innovative set of agronomic practices to increase cane yields significantly. This system was initiated in the year 2009 for improvement in sugarcane agriculture. The initiation of this method was a joint venture of ICRISAT and WWF.

                                                                                                                • Sugarcane breeding/crop improvement is carried out through multiple research station/centres across India; Coimbatore (ICAR-SBI) is one major centre. Sugarcane breeding Institute was established in 1912 in Coimbatore (Tamil Nadu). On 1 April 1969, it was made a part of ICAR.
                                                                                                                Oilseeds: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                • Oilseeds are produced for extracting edible oils Major oilseed crops are Toria, Mustard, Sesame (til), Linseed, castor seed, Sunflower, Soybean etc.
                                                                                                                • Yellow Revolution is associated with the increase in the production of oilseed crops. Oil and oil cake obtained from oilseeds are used in varnish, lubricant, candle, soap, fertilizer, aromatic substance etc.
                                                                                                                • According to Economic Survey, 2025-26 data, total oilseed production in India in 2024-25 has been 30.4 million tonnes.
                                                                                                                • The largest producer of total oilseeds in India is Rajasthan followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
                                                                                                                • Peanut is a major oilseed crop. Peanuts are a good source of vegetable protein. Peanuts are a tropical crop. 50 to 125 cm of average annual rainfall and 15°C to 25°C of temperature are sufficient for growing this crop. Peanut is also known as Cashew nut of Poor.
                                                                                                                • Pegging is a useful phenomenon in groundnut. In pegging, after fertilization, the pegs of the faded flower come out and enter the soil which grows quite close to the taproot. Once it penetrates the soil, the peg turns horizontal and continues to grow and mature into a peanut. For the cultivation of Peanut, the soil must have the enrichment of the gypsum.
                                                                                                                • According to 2024-25 figure, the three leading Ground nut producing states in India are –

                                                                                                                1. Gujarat (5.22 Million Tonnes)

                                                                                                                2. Rajasthan (2.14 Million Tonnes)

                                                                                                                3. Madhya Pradesh (1.55 Million Tonnes)

                                                                                                                • Soyabean is a good source of protein in addition to the food oil. Favourable condition for soyabean cultivation are temperature ranging between 15-25°C, average annual rainfall of 40-60 cm and loamy soil with a ph ranging between 6-6.5.
                                                                                                                • Soyabean is a cultivated as a Kharifcrop generally sown in June and harvested in October. This crop requires irrigation 3 to 4 times.
                                                                                                                • According to data from SOPA for, 2025 in India, 48.642 Lakh hectare area of Madhya Pradesh is cropped under soyabean which is 42.46% of total cropping area of Soyabean in India.
                                                                                                                • The three leading producer states of Soyabean as per Economic Survey 2025-26, In the year 2024-25 are–

                                                                                                                1. Maharashtra (7.37 Million tonnes)

                                                                                                                2. Madhya Pradesh (5.38 Million tonnes)

                                                                                                                3. Rajasthan (1.18 Million tonnes)

                                                                                                                • Mustard is also a major oilseed crop. It is a Rabi crop. For the cultivation of mustard the temperature ranging between 15-25°C and an annual rainfall of 75-100 cm is required.

                                                                                                                It is sown in the month of October-November and harvested in the months of February-March.

                                                                                                                • According to the Economic Survey 2025-26 data, in the year 2024-25, Rajasthan is first in Rapeseeds & Mustard Production in India followed by Uttar Pradesh (2nd) and Haryana (3rd). The major varieties of mustard are pusa bold, Pusa, Jai kisan and Varuna. Pitambari is a species of yellow mustard (RYSK-05-02).

                                                                                                                      Pulses: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                      • Pulses are a major source of protein in India. The major pulse crops of India are gram, urad, green gram, mash, tur, lentils etc. These crops have the capacity of nitrogen fixation from the air. Cobalt is known to be essential for symbiotic nitrogen fixation by Rhizobium. Cobalt is also needed in the synthesis of vitamin B₁₂.
                                                                                                                      • According to data of the Economic Survey 2025-26, in the year 2024-25, the largest producer of total pulses in India is Madhya Pradesh which is followed by Maharashtra (2nd) and Rajasthan (3rd).

                                                                                                                      Malviya chamtkar is a species of tur dal. Other species are Amar, Aajad, Bahar, Malviya vikash, MA6, Paras etc.

                                                                                                                      • Most productive state of gram in India is Madhya Pradesh. The NPK ratio for Pulse crop is 0: 1: 1, 1: 2: 2 or 1: 2: 3.
                                                                                                                      'Silk': key facts from the book
                                                                                                                      • India is the second largest producer of silk in the world after China.
                                                                                                                      • Mulberry Silk, Tasar Silk, Muga Silk and Eri Silk are four types of natural Silk produced in India.
                                                                                                                      • Chemically silk is made up of a protein secreted by cat erpillar famously known as Silkworm. These Silkworms thrives on some special plants and they develop a cocoon like protective layer around them for their survival.
                                                                                                                      • Life cycle of Silkworm consists of four stages:-

                                                                                                                      Egg, Caterpillar, Pupa, Moth.

                                                                                                                      • To obtain silk the silkworms are prevented from reaching the moth stage by killing the larva putting them into boiling water so as to save the Cocoon from breaking, from which the commercially important continuous fibre of Silk is obtained which is used for weaving Silk clothes.
                                                                                                                      • According to the data released in the annual report of the Central Silk Board, 2023-24, Karnataka is the largest silk producing state in India, followed by Andhra Pradesh.
                                                                                                                      • Karnataka is major producer of Mulberry Silk. Here

                                                                                                                      44.15% of Mulberry Silk is produced. Karnataka also produces 41.69% of total raw silk produced in India (2023-24).

                                                                                                                      • Andhra Pradesh stands second after Karnataka by producing

                                                                                                                      35.08% of total raw silk produced in India.

                                                                                                                      • Assam is the major producer of Muga Silk producing a total of 65.07% of Muga silk produced in India.
                                                                                                                      • Eri Silk is produced mostly in Assam. Assam & BTC share

                                                                                                                      56.56% of total Eri Silk production in India.

                                                                                                                      • Tasar Silk is classified into two categories Tropical and Oak Tasar. Jharkhand produces most of India’s Tropical Tasar (2023-24) while Manipur is the major producer of Oak Tasar in India. Whereas Tasar Silk as a whole is produced mostly in Jharkhand (2023-24).
                                                                                                                      Plantation Crops: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                      (i) Coffee

                                                                                                                      • Coffee in India is grown under a canopy of thick natural shade in ecologically sensitive regions of the Western and Eastern Ghats. This is one of the 36 biodiversity hotspots of the world. Coffee contributes significantly to sustaining the unique bio-diversity of the region and is also responsible for the socio-economic development in the remote, hilly areas. In India, coffee is traditionally grown in the Western Ghats in Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Coffee cultivation is also expanding rapidly in the nontraditional areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as well as in the North East State. In India coffee was firstly grown in Chikkamagaluru district of Karnataka.
                                                                                                                      • Arabica and Robusta are the two varieties of coffee grown in India.
                                                                                                                      • Average annual temperature ranging between 15ºC to 18ºC and average annual precipitation of 150-250 cm is favourable for Coffee Cultivation.
                                                                                                                      • Loamy soil or soil made from lava is perfect for coffee cultivation and it is grown on hilly slopes.
                                                                                                                      • According to the data from coffee Board Government of India, in the Year 2024-25, Karnataka is the highest coffee producing state of India.
                                                                                                                      • According to the figures of the year 2024-25 (Final Estimate), India produced a total of 363500 MTs of coffee, of which 256000 MTs is produced from Karnataka only.
                                                                                                                      • Kerala produces 72950 MTs of India’s coffee and is a second largest coffee producing state in India.
                                                                                                                      • Tamil Nadu stands at third place in coffee production which is 19275 MTs of total.
                                                                                                                      • Coffee is amplified through seeds.
                                                                                                                      • National Horticulture Board was set up by Government of India in April 1984. The National Horticluture Board is registered as an autonomous society under the Societies Registration Act 1860, with its headquarters in Gurugram(Haryana).
                                                                                                                      • Coffee Board in India was established by Government of India under section VII of the Statute “Coffee Act, 1942”. Ministry of Commerce and Industry has administrative control of this Board.

                                                                                                                      Plantation Crops · Tea and Rubber: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                      • Tea is the most important plantation crop in India. Tea owes its origin to the ‘Yunnan’ plateau of South China.
                                                                                                                      • Tea is a crop of Tropical region. Tea requires temperature ranging between 25ºC to 30ºC (temperature less than 15ºC and frost are dangerous for tea) is required for proper growth.
                                                                                                                      • Tea requires 150-200 cm of annual rainfall and is grown on hilly slopes.
                                                                                                                      • In India there are two main types of Tea:- (i) Bohea or Chinese

                                                                                                                      (ii) Assamica or Assamese.

                                                                                                                      • According to annual data of Tea Board India, Assam is the largest tea (2024-25) producing state of India. According to figures of 2024-25 (Final data), Assam is at the top both in terms of Area under cultivation and tea production.
                                                                                                                      • Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka are major tea producing states of India.
                                                                                                                      • Tea consumption has grown particularly rapidly in China, India and other emerging economies, driven by a combination of higher incomes and diversification in to other marker segments, such as organic and specially teas.
                                                                                                                      • According to figures (FAO) for the year 2024, China is ranked first in the world in tea (leaves) production followed by India at Second, Kenya at third and Sri Lanka at fourth place.
                                                                                                                      • According to figures (FAO) of year 2024 top tea exporting countries are:

                                                                                                                      1. Kenya, 2. China, 3. India, 4. Sri Lanka.

                                                                                                                      • Plant of rubber requires hot and humid climatic conditions.
                                                                                                                      • Temperature ranging between 25ºC to 28ºC, average annual rainfall of 300 cm is necessary for rubber plant growth.
                                                                                                                      • Kerala is the largest rubber producing state of India. According to figures of2014-15, 78.71% of total rubber production of In dia takes place in Kerala. Ernakulam, Kottayam, Kozhikode and Kollam are major rubber producing districts of Kerala.
                                                                                                                      • Top five states of India in terms of rubber production (2024-25) are -

                                                                                                                      1. Kerala 2. Tripura 3. Karnataka 4. Assam 5. Tamil Nadu.

                                                                                                                      • According to FAO 2024 India is placed 6th in the world in terms of natural rubber production.
                                                                                                                      • According to FAO: 2024 Thailand produces the largest amount of natural rubber in primary forms in the world.
                                                                                                                      Plantation Crops · Other Plantation Crops: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                      • According to agriculture ministry plantation crops includes Coconut, Arecanut, Cocoa, Cashewnut, Oil Palm and Palmyrah. Whereas according to commerce ministry plantation crop includes Coconut, Arecanut, Cocoa, Cashewnut, Oil palm Palmyrah, Tea, Coffee and Rubber are Plantation crops of India.
                                                                                                                      • According to data of Agricultural Statistics at a Glance, 2024-25 Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of tobacco among all states of India. According to figures of the year 2024-25, 48.57% of tobacco production of India takes place in Uttar Pradesh.
                                                                                                                      • According to figures of the year 2024-25 major tobacco producing states of India are -

                                                                                                                      Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka.

                                                                                                                      • State having the largest area of land under tobacco cultivation in India (in 2024-25) are Gujarat (204.79 thousand hectares), Andhra Pradesh (139 thousand hectares), Karnataka (79 thousand hectares), Uttar Pradesh (33.29 thousand hectares) and West Bengal (12.3 thousand hectares).
                                                                                                                      • According to the data of Agricultural Statistics at a Glance, 2024-25 top three Coconut producing states in the year 2024-25 (3rd A.E.) are:

                                                                                                                      1. Tamil Nadu (30%), 2. Kerala (27%) and Karnataka (25%). Tamil Nadu is the highest producer of Coconut in India.

                                                                                                                      • Globally Indonesia, India and Philippines are major Coconut (in shell) producing countries in 2024.
                                                                                                                      • Many types of Spices are grown in ‘Kerala’ that is why it is also called as ‘Garden of Spices;
                                                                                                                      • According to figures of the year 2024-25 (3rd A.E.), Madhya Pradesh is the top producer of spices.
                                                                                                                      • From ancient times, Kerala has been famous in the world for its production of spices.
                                                                                                                      • Cloves are the flower-buds of medium–sized evergreen plant of Eugenia caryophyllata family. It is a variety of spicies having medicinal significance too. According to the figures of the year 2024-25 (P) (Final data), clove is cultivated in Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.
                                                                                                                      • According to figures of annual report 2024-25, top three state in Arecanut production are - 1. Karnataka, 2. Kerala and 3. Assam.
                                                                                                                      • Top three Cashew nut producer states (in 2024-25) of India are- Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
                                                                                                                      • Black pepper is also known as black gold. It thrives in a hot and humid climate, with annual rainfall around 200 cm and hilly sloped with altitude ranging between 1100 to 1300 meters. It requires an average annual temperature between 15ºC to 30ºC.
                                                                                                                      • According to data Agricultural Statistics at a Glance 2024- 25, in the year 2024-25 (3rd A.E.) top three spice producing states of India are 1. Madhya Pradesh, 2. Andhra Pradesh,

                                                                                                                      3. Gujarat.

                                                                                                                      • According to figures of 2022 India is the second largest producer of Black Pepper after Vietnam.
                                                                                                                      Jhuming Agriculture: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                      • Shifting cultivation is a practice in which an area of forest is cleared and cultivated by tribes and when the fertility of that area degrades the people shift to other places until its fertility has been naturally restored. It is known by different names in different regions such as Jhum in the north-eastern state, Pondu in Odisha, Kumari in Western Ghats etc.

                                                                                                                      KumariWestern Ghats

                                                                                                                            Agriculture : Miscellaneous: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                            According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, as per data for 2024-25, total food grain production in India is estimated at a record 357.7 million tonnes.

                                                                                                                            • According to the Final Estimates for 2024-25 in India, the production of rice is 150.2 million tonnes, production of wheat is 117.9 million tonnes, production of nutri/coarse cereals (Includes Maize, Jowar, Ragi, Bajra, Small Millets and Barley) is 63.9 million tonnes and production of pulses is 25.7 million tonne.
                                                                                                                            • According to figures 2024-25 Uttar Pradesh is top food grain producing state with a share of 17.85% in total food grain production of the country. In this context, Madhya Pradesh (13.04%) is at second and Punjab (9.16%) is at third place.
                                                                                                                            • National Research Centre for Banana was established by Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) on August 21, 1993. This centre works on four major thrust areas of research viz., crop improvement, crop production, post harvest management and crop protection. According to the figures of 2023-24 (Final) three leading states in the production of Banana in India are Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu respectively.
                                                                                                                            • The botanical name of Maize is 'Zea Mays'. It is a major food crop. Due to its compatibility to diverse agro-climatic conditions, it can be sown throughout the year. At the global level, it is called as the “Queen of cereals”. Maize is used in the production of starch products such as starch powder, Dextrin, Seatex etc. Besides this, maize oil is also used for the production of Bio-Diesel.
                                                                                                                            • Many types of alcoholic drinks such as whisky (American Alcohol), Cauim (Beer of Brazil), etc are also prepared by using maize.
                                                                                                                            • In India, Maize is the third largest foodgrain crop in production and consumption after rice and wheat. The maturity period of maize is almost 90 to 150 days depending on season and region. The maturity period of Maize in the state of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh etc. is about 90 to 150 days.
                                                                                                                            • According to Economic Survey 2025-26 the three leading Maize producing states 2024-25 in India are Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Bihar respectively.
                                                                                                                            • Shaktiman-I and Shaktiman-II are genetically hybrid varieties of Maize.
                                                                                                                            • The credit is given to Frederick Wilson to start farming of kidney bean and potato in the Bhagirathi valley. In the 19th century, he was the first man to settle permanently in the Bhagirathi Valley. He was given the nickname of Pahari and the king of Harshil.
                                                                                                                            • According to the data of Agricultural Statistics at a glance, 2024-25 in the year 2024-25 (3rd A.E.), Uttar Pradesh is the largest producer of Potato in the country, about 58108 Thousand M.T. of the country’s total production of Potato is produced in U.P. followed by West Bengal and Bihar respectively.
                                                                                                                            • The best variety of potatoes for processing is kufri chip Sona-2. Chipsona-3 is the best variety of potatoes for processing in plains and Kufri Him Sona is the best variety of Potatoes for processing in hilly areas.
                                                                                                                            • The climate of lower Ganga plains contains high temperature with high humidity. Paddy and Jute crops are most suitable for this type of climate. Jute is produced in an alluvial loamy soil. In India, West Bengal is the largest producer (2024-25) of Jute & Mesta followed by Bihar and Assam. It is known as the ‘golden fibre’. Mesta is an allied bast fibre crop belonging to the genus Hibiscus (family Malvaceae). According to data 2024-25, West Bengal (0.43 million hectares) has the largest Jute & Mesta cultivated area in India.
                                                                                                                            • In the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, Saffron is produced on a commercial level. It is also called as Zafran. The other saffron producing countries except India are Spain, Iran, Greece and Italy. Green hair desease is found in Millets.
                                                                                                                            • For the cultivation of onion, first seeds are planted and small plants are prepared and later those plants are transplanted. As per 2024-25 (3rd A.E.) data, the onion leading three states of India are Maharashtra (44%), Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.
                                                                                                                            • According to the National Horticulture Board 2024-25 (Final) in India, the main mango producing states are Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka and Gujarat respectively.
                                                                                                                            • Sindhu is a seedless variety of mango. This is the only seedless mango variety of the world.
                                                                                                                            • Aamrapali variety of Mango was developed by the Indian Agriculture research institute Pusa in the year 1971 by hybridisation of Dashehari and Neelam varieties of Mango.
                                                                                                                            • Lalit and Banarasi are the advance varieties of Guava. This variety of Guava is developed by Indian Institute of Horticulture Research.
                                                                                                                            • Indian Gooseberry has medicinal significance. Kanchan, Krishna and Banarasi are improved varieties of Indian Gooseberry (Amla). Vitamin Cis abundantly found in it.
                                                                                                                            • Stem of ginger which grows in the soil and stores food is known as the rhizome.
                                                                                                                            • Lobia, Moong and Arhar are used as food, fodder and Pulses.
                                                                                                                            • Groundnut, sesame and Bajra are grown in dry Agricultural regions. Irrigation of these crops totally depends on rain.
                                                                                                                            • The main objective of National Food Security Mission is to increase the production of rice, wheat and pulses through area expansion and productivity enhancement in a sustainable manner in identified districts of the country restoring soil fertility and productivity at individual farm level; creation of employment opportunities and enhancing farm level economy (i.e., farm profits) to restore confidence among farmers.
                                                                                                                            • India and Pakistan produce about 80% of the world total production of cluster bean. After proving the importance of Guar Gum in the extraction of Shale gas, a tremendous increase in its demand has been recorded. Guar Gum is extracted from the seeds of cluster Bean.
                                                                                                                            • According to the data Handbook on Fisheries Statistics, 2023 released by Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandary and Dairying for the year 2022-23 the leading Inland and Marine fish producing states are-

                                                                                                                            (1) Andhra Pradesh (51.06 Lakh Tonnes) (2) West Bengal (20.45 Lakh Tonnes) (3) Karnataka (12.25 Lakh Tonnes),

                                                                                                                            (4) Odisha (10.52 Lakh Tonnes) and (5) Kerala (9.21 Lakh Tonnes). Freshwater fish production is largest produced in Andhra Pradesh.

                                                                                                                            • Arunachal Pradesh is emerging as a major tourist destination in north-eastern India. There is a very rich biodiversity of flora and fauna. The state is famous for Green forests, wild life diversity, deep river valleys and beautiful plateau. It is home to a different variety of orchid.

                                                                                                                            Sikkim achieved the status of India’s first biological / organic state. It is notable that producing crops based on organic fertilizers completely or in other words without using pesticides or chemical fertilizers is called organic farming. Borlaug Award is given in the field of Agricultural Science. This award was started in the year 1972 after the name of Nobel Prize Winner Norman. E. Borlaug.

                                                                                                                                  Animal Husbandry: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Animal Husbandry refers to the management and care of animals for purposes such as obtaining food, fiber, labor and other products. It includes practices to improve the quality and productivity of livestock through breeding, feeding and disease control. As per 21th Livestock census total livestock population is 536.76 million in the country showing an increase of 4.8% over Livestock Census 2012. The total livestock population in Rural and Urban area is 514.11 million and 22.65 million respectively with percentage share of 95.78% for Rural and 4.22% for Urban area. The total livestock population in Rural area has increased by 4.56% and in Urban area the increase is 11.19%.

                                                                                                                                  (i) Milch Breeds - The cow of this breed give more milk but the Bull are not good for agricultural work and load vehicle. It includes major breeds like Gir, Sahiwal, Sindhi, Devni, Tharpakar, etc.

                                                                                                                                  (ii)Draught Breeds - It includes breeds like Nagori, Bhalavi, Hallikar, Kangayam, Khillar, Ponwar and Siri etc.

                                                                                                                                  • The country’s best indigenous cow breeds are found in Rajasthan. The cows breed found in Rajasthan are Tharparkar, Rathi, Kankrej, Sahiwal, Lal Sindhi, Gir, Nagauri, Haryanvi, Malvi and Mewati.
                                                                                                                                  • Sahiwal cow breeds is mainly found in Sindh province of Pakistan. Its milking capacity is quite high.

                                                                                                                                  There are many breeds of buffalo. They mainly include Murrah, Bhadawari, Zafara badi, Suttari, Mehsana, Nagpuri, Nili Ravi, Pandharpuri etc.

                                                                                                                                  • According to Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2024,in India, maximum sheep are found in Telangana in 2019. The best quality of sheep breed of the country are found in the valley of Kashmir, Kullu, Chamba and Kangra.
                                                                                                                                  • Goat is known as the “Poor man's cow”. Milk, meat, leather and wool are obtained from the goats. In India, they are the main source of meat. The highest milk yielding breed of goat in India is Jamunapari. It is also considered as good for both milk and meat. It producer about 2.5-3.0 kg milk everyday.
                                                                                                                                  • According to data of Basic Animal, Husbandry Statistics 2025, the total meat production in the country is 10.50 million tonnes during 2024-25. The meat production has increased by 2.46% in 2024-25 as compared to previous year. The top 5 meat producing states are West Bengal (12.46%), Uttar Pradesh (12.20%), Maharashtra (11.57%), Andhra Pradesh (10.84%) and Telangana (10.49%).

                                                                                                                                  In India, the white revolution was started in July, 1970 with the launch of operation flood-I Plan. Dr. Verghese Kurien is known as the father of the white revolution in India. White revolution is related to milk production. According to production data of Food and Agriculture Organization Corporate Statistical Database (FAOSTAT), India is the highest milk (Raw milk of cattle) producer i.e., rank first position in the world contributing 16.93% of global milk production in the year 2024. According to Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, total milk production in the country is 247.87 million tonnes during 2024-25. The per capita availability of milk is 485 grams per day. The average yield per animal per day for exotic crossbred is 9.05 kg/ day/Animal and for indigenous/non-descript is 3.86 kg/ day/Animal. Top 5 milk producing states are Uttar Pradesh (15.66%), Rajasthan (14.82%), Madhya Pradesh (9.12%), Gujarat (7.78%), Maharashtra (6.71%). Operation Flood was started to increase the production of milk. Its first phase was from 1970 to 80, the second phase from 1981to 85 and the third phase from 1985 to 1996. The total egg production in India during 2024-25 is 149.11 billion numbers. The top 5 egg-producing states are Andhra Pradesh (18.37%), Tamil Nadu (15.63%), Telangana (12.98%), West Bengal (10.72%) and Karnataka (6.67%).

                                                                                                                                  • In the year 1970, Indian Dairy corporation was established in Baroda (Vadodara) Gujarat. Its aim was to make Operation Flood successful. National Dairy Development Board was established in 1965. Dr. Verghese Kurien was the founder of the National Dairy Development Board and the Indian Dairy Corporation.

                                                                                                                                  National Dairy Research Institute is located in Karnal, Haryana. It was given the status of Deemed University in 1989. Bihar has the highest animal density in India. In the context of total livestock in 2019, Uttar Pradesh was at the top and Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh were placed at second and third respectively. In the context of cattle stock, the top three states are West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

                                                                                                                                  Mineral Resources: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                  (A) Rock System

                                                                                                                                  • India has fairly rich and varied mineral resources. However, these are unevenly distributed. Peninsular rock contains most of the reserves of coal, metallic minerals, mica and many other non-metallic minerals.
                                                                                                                                  • Sedimentary rocks in the western and eastern portions of the peninsula, in Gujarat and Assam have most of the petroleum deposits.
                                                                                                                                  • Rajasthan with the rock system of the peninsula, has reserves of many non-ferrous minerals.
                                                                                                                                  • The vast alluvial plains of North India are almost devoid of economic minerals. These variations exist largely because of the differences in the geological structure, processes and time evolved in the formation of minerals.
                                                                                                                                  • Vindhya Range of rocks is actually sedimentary rocks formed by the sedimentation of water suspended particles. Among these rocks, the prominent minerals are limestone, sand, china clay, etc.
                                                                                                                                  • Geologists define mineral as a “homogeneous naturally occurring substance with a definable internal structure”.
                                                                                                                                  • Dharwar system is considered to be the storehouse of the metallic minerals and hence has a high economic significance. This system of rocks is rich in metallic minerals such as iron, manganese, gold, copper, etc. This system is mainly found in Aravallis, Chotanagpur plateau, Meghalaya, Tamil Nadu, etc.
                                                                                                                                  • The largest reserves of mineral resources in India are found in the Peninsular region. It is often called as the Heart-place of Indian minerals. According to annual report 2024-25, India produces as many as 95 minerals, which includes 4 fuel, 10 metallic, 23 non-metallic, 3 atomic and 55 minor minerals (including building and other materials). The total value of mineral production (excluding atomic Minor Minerals & fuel minerals) during 2024-25 has been estimated at Rs. 141061 crore, which shows an decrease of about 0.7% over that of the previous year. During 2024-25, estimated value for metallic mineral is Rs. 128261 crores or 91% of the total value and non-metallic minerals (excluding Minor Minerals) is Rs. 12800 crores or 9% of the total value. For the year 2024-25, the estimated mineral production (excluding Atomic, Fuel and Minor Minerals) would be from 20 states of which the bulk of value of mineral production of about 97.70% was confined to 8 States only. The order was Odisha with a share of 43.49% followed by Rajasthan (16.26%), Chhattisgarh (13.69), Karnataka (12.42%), Maharashtra (4.76%), Jharkhand (3.26%), Madhya Pradesh (2.78%) and Andhra Pradesh (1.04%) in the total value of mineral production. The principal mineral producing states, which have indicated an increase in the value of mineral producing during 2023-24 with respect to 2022-23 are Maharashtra (64.49%), Uttarakhand (49.8%), Bihar (26.12%), Karnataka (20.12%), Odisha (17.23%), Madhya Pradesh (16.3%), Meghalaya (15.21%), Andhra Pradesh (13.56%), Jharkhand (12.78%), Tamil Nadu (11.86%), Himachal Pradesh (9.59%), Chhattisgarh (8.55%), Assam (7.6%), Jammu and Kashmir (5.14%), Rajasthan (4.88%), Gujarat (4.33%) and Uttar Pradesh (1.7%).
                                                                                                                                  Mineral Resources · Iron-Ore: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Iron Ores in India are majorly found in Dharwar rock system. Dharwar Rock System is economically most important rock system found in India.

                                                                                                                                  Haematite and magnetite are the most important Iron Ores in India. About 79% haematite ore deposites are found in the Eastern Sector (Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh) while about 93% magnetite ore deposits occur in Southern Sector (Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu). Karnataka alone contributes 72% of magnetite deposits in India. Ofthese, haematite is considered to be superior because of its higher grade. Indian deposites of haematite belong to the Precambrian Iron Ore Series and the Ore is within banded iron ore formations occurring as massive, laminated, friable and also in powdery form.

                                                                                                                                  • The high-quality iron ore (Haematite and Magnetite) is explored from Bailadila Mine of Chhattisgarh. Bailadila Mine is the largest mechanized mine of India. Iron ore explored from this mine is exported to Japan from Vishakhapatnam Port.

                                                                                                                                  India: Major Iron

                                                                                                                                  Ore Fields

                                                                                                                                  • Kudremukh is a famous mine of Iron ore in Karnataka. Magnetite iron ore is majorly found in Karnataka.
                                                                                                                                  • Nathara Ki Pal and Thur - Hundera region of Udaipur are famous for Iron ore in Rajasthan.
                                                                                                                                  • According to Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2024 Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Goa, which chronologically have the largest (till April 1, 2020) reserves/ resources of iron ores (Magnetite) in India.
                                                                                                                                  • Haematite ore in India is concentrated over the states of Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Goa chronologically have largest (till April 1, 2020) Reserves/ resources in India.
                                                                                                                                  • According to Indian Minerals Year Book, 2024 in 2023 India is placed at 3rd largest in the world in terms of iron ore production.
                                                                                                                                  Mineral Resources · Zinc: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Zinc is generally found in the combined form with lead from the sulphides of Zinc. It is used to prevent rusting in iron, making an alloy, Electrodes, Motor parts, dry batteries, etc.
                                                                                                                                  • The State of Rajasthan has a monopoly in the production and reserves of Zinc.
                                                                                                                                  • Best quality Zinc and Lead reserves of Asia are found in Rampur Agucha region of Bhilwara District.
                                                                                                                                  • Zawar region (Udaipur District) in Rajasthan is the largest zinc producing area in India. Other deposits of zinc in Rajasthan are - Rajpur Debari region (Udaipur), Dungarpur, Alwar, Banswada, and Sirohi.
                                                                                                                                  • Minor deposits of zinc in India are found in Bhotang region (Sikkim), Riyasi (Jammu and Kashmir), Almora and Tehri Garhwal (Uttarakhand).
                                                                                                                                  • Hindustan Zinc Limited has established super smelter system that works for the melting of zinc and lead with the help of Britain in Rampur Agucha region.
                                                                                                                                  Mineral Resources · Silver: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Silver is generally found combined with Lead, Zinc and Copper from acidic igneous rocks. As per the figures of 2023-24 (P), Rajasthan is the largest producer of Silver.
                                                                                                                                  • Second leading state is Karnataka. According to Indian Minerals yearbook 2024, the total reserves/resources of silver in the country as of April 1, 2020 in terms of metal content was estimated at 30267.91 tonnes, of which 7707.07 tonnes are under 'Reserves' and 22560.84 tonnes are under the 'Remaining Resources'.
                                                                                                                                  • By States, Rajasthan accounted for about 86.29% reserves/ resources in terms of ore while Karnataka with 4.56%, Jharkhand with 4.19% and Andhra Pradesh 2.98% were among the States next in the order. Madhya Pradesh with, Uttarakhand, Odisha, Meghalaya, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra together shared 1.98% of the ore reserves/ remaining resources.
                                                                                                                                  • Zawar Mines is famous for silver production in Rajasthan.
                                                                                                                                  • Kolar and Hutti Gold Mines are famous for gold deposits in Karnataka.
                                                                                                                                  Mineral Resources · Copper: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Copper is found in veins of Dharwar rocks of India. According to Indian Minerals Yearbook 2024, largest reserves/resources (as on 1/4/2020) of copper ore are in Rajasthan (52.25%), followed by Madhya Pradesh (23.28%) and Jharkhand (15.14%).
                                                                                                                                  • The remaining 9.33% are distributed across Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Odisha, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. Three major districts of copper ore deposits are Jhunjhunu (Rajasthan), Balaghat (M.P.) and Singhbhum (Jharkhand).

                                                                                                                                  (1) Madhya Pradesh (2545820 tonnes)
