                                                                                                                                  • Hindustan Copper Limited, a public sector company, controls most of the copper production in India.
                                                                                                                                  Mineral Resources · Bauxite: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Bauxite is an ore of aluminium. Its colour varies from white-pink to red depending on the quantity of iron content.
                                                                                                                                  • Bauxite is found in the laterite rocks of the tertiary period. It is mainly used in the production of alumina and aluminium. Originally bauxite is hydrated aluminium oxide.
                                                                                                                                  • As per the figures of the year 2024 Indian Minerals Yearbook, Odisha is the largest (2023-24, P) producer (73.56%) as well as the state having the largest reserves/ resources (as of 1/04/2022) of bauxite (41.49%). Major bauxite resources are concentrated in the East Coast Bauxite deposited in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh.
                                                                                                                                  • Bauxite in Odisha is obtained from the rocks of Khondalite ranges. This is found in the Koraput and Raigarh regions.
                                                                                                                                  • In Gujarat, it is mainly found in Dwarka and Devbhumi. Lohardaga, Gumla and Latehar are the major bauxite regions of Jharkhand.
                                                                                                                                  • The production of bauxite at 23968 thousand tonnes in 2023-24 increased by 1% compared to the previous year. NALCO is the leading producer of bauxite and contributed 31% of the total production. The share of Public Sector mines was about 46% of the total production in 2023-24.
                                                                                                                                  • Leading bauxite producing states as per the figures of 2023-24 (P) are

                                                                                                                                  1. Odisha (17591967 Tonnes)

                                                                                                                                  2. Jharkhand (2043734 Tonnes)

                                                                                                                                  3. Gujarat (1643130 Tonnes)

                                                                                                                                  4. Maharashtra (1058581 Tonnes)

                                                                                                                                  5. Chhattisgarh (1033176 Tonnes)

                                                                                                                                  Mineral Resources · Tin: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Tin is one of the earliest metals known and used mainly in bronze implements. It is a scarce element with an incidence of about 2 PPM in the earth's crust. Tin is used mostly for tin plating, soldering special alloys and in the production of bronze. Tin ore is known as Cassiterite. Tin reserves are limited in India. Chhattisgarh is the only state producing tin in India. According to data from Indian Minerals Yearbook 2024, major reserves/resources (as on 1/04/2020) of tin ore are found in Haryana, Chhattisgarh and Odisha.
                                                                                                                                  • The production of tin concentrates in 2023-24 (P) was at 22345 kg., as against 45432 kg. in the preceding year. All companies (1 public sector and 3 private sectors) related to tin mines reported production in 2023-24 (P). All these mines are located in Chhattisgarh.
                                                                                                                                  Non-Metallic Minerals · Mica: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Mica is a flexible, transparent and thermal electro-resistor. As per the Govt. of India Notification S.O. 423 (E), dated 10th February, 2015 'mica' has been declared as a 'Minor Mineral'. It is found in igneous metamorphic and sedimentary rocks.
                                                                                                                                  • According to data from Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022, Rajasthan is the largest producer of mica.
                                                                                                                                  • According to Minerals Yearbook 2021, the total reserves/ resources (as of 1/04/2015) of mica in India are shared between - Andhra Pradesh (41%), Rajasthan (28%), Odisha (17%), Maharashtra (13%) and Bihar (2%).
                                                                                                                                  • The largest mica chain is found across Hazaribag, Gaya and Munger. Koderma district falls in this chain which is also known as the capital of mica.
                                                                                                                                  Non-Metallic Minerals · Marble: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                  • Marble is a 'Minor Mineral' as defined under clause (e) of section 3 of the Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act, 1957.
                                                                                                                                  • The term "marble" is derived from the Latin word "Murmur", which in turn is said to have been coined from the Greek word "Mormorous", meaning shining stone.
                                                                                                                                  • Marble is a type of metamorphic rock that is formed from sedimentary carbonate rocks by contact metamorphism. Marble is metamorphosed from dolostone or sedimentary carbonate rocks.
                                                                                                                                  • Makrana is situated in Nagaur district in Rajasthan.
                                                                                                                                  • High-quality marble is found here. This marble is used in the Taj Mahal and Victoria Memorial (Kolkata).
                                                                                                                                  • Polishing and cutting factory of marble is situated in Katni (M.P.).
                                                                                                                                  • According to data from Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022, Rajasthan is the largest producer of marble in India.

                                                                                                                                        Energy Mineral · Coal: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                        • Coal is solid sedimentary rock mainly constituted of hydrocarbons. Coal is mainly used as a fuel producing heat and energy. It is remains of organic matter and animal fossils accumulated in sedimentary rock by a different methods.
                                                                                                                                        • Coal occurs in rock series of two main geological ages-

                                                                                                                                        (1) Gondwana (2) Tertiary

                                                                                                                                        • Gondwana coal is high quality coal with low ash content. while tertiary coal is low quality coal. Most of the coal produced in India is obtained from this region. Bituminous coal is abundantly found here. It has low sulfur content. The coalfields of India, most coalfields are related to Lower Gondwana. More than about 99% of coal deposits and production have been covered by Gondwana coal.
                                                                                                                                        • Major Coalfields of Gondwana System are - Damodar Valley Coalfield, Son Valley Coalfield, Mahanadi Valley Coalfield, Godavari Coalfield, Satpura Coalfield, Vardha Ghati Coalfield and Rajmahal Coalfield.

                                                                                                                                        Map not to scale

                                                                                                                                        • Raniganj coalfield of West Bengal is situated in the upper Damodar valley which is the largest and the most important coalfield of India.
                                                                                                                                        • Coal is found in a variety of forms depending on the degree of compression and the depth and time ofburial.
                                                                                                                                        • There are four major categories of coal based on the carbon content and impurity –

                                                                                                                                        (1) Peat

                                                                                                                                        (2) Lignite

                                                                                                                                        (3) Bituminous

                                                                                                                                        (4) Anthracite

                                                                                                                                        • Carbon content in peat is less than 25%.
                                                                                                                                        • Carbon content in lignite coal is up to 25-35%. Carbon content in bituminous coal is up to 45-86%. Carbon content in anthracite coal is up to 86-97%.
                                                                                                                                        • Neyveli in Tamil Nadu is a principal lignite reserve.
                                                                                                                                        • Coal that has been buried deep and subjected to increased temperature is bituminous coal. It is the most popular coal in commercial use.
                                                                                                                                        • Anthracite is the high quality hard coal. According to the National Coal Inventory of 2025, published by Geological Survey of India based on resources estimated by CMPDI, GSI, MECL, SCCL and some private/public enterpreneurs, a maximum depth up to 1200m.; the total estimated coal reserve (resources) of India is 400.715 billion tonnes as of April 1, 2025. With continuous exploration effort in 64 coal field (45 Gondwana & 19 Tertiary Coalfield) and 15 lignite field have resulted in substantial augmentation of the geological resources of coal and lignite. As 1st April, 2025 total updated geological coal and lignite resources of the country stand at 400.715 billion tonnes and 47.37 billion tonnes respectively.
                                                                                                                                        • According to data of Ministry of coal reserves/resources (as on 1st April, 2023) are found chronologically in Odisha (100.99 Billion tonnes), Jharkhand (93.25 Billion tonnes), Chhattisgarh (85.26 Billion tonnes), West Bengal (34.39 Billion tonnes), and Madhya Pradesh (33.56 Billion tonnes).
                                                                                                                                        • The total production of coal reported in 2024-25 was 1047.523 million tonnes. Odisha is the largest coal producing state with a share of about 25.71%, followed by Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh having a contribution of 19.68% and

                                                                                                                                        19.56% respectively in the national output. Next in order of share in the production were Madhya Pradesh (15.99%), Telangana (6.83%), Maharashtra (6.76%), West Bengal (3.44%) and Uttar Pradesh (1.99%).

                                                                                                                                        • The share of coking coal in the total coal (2024-25) produced in India is 6.35% and the rest 93.65% is non coking coal.
                                                                                                                                        • Major coal fields of Jharkhand are Jharia, North Karnapura, South Karnapura, Bokaro, Chandrapura, Rajmahal, Giridih, etc.
                                                                                                                                        • Jharia coalfield is situated in Dhanbad district of Jharkhand. Major coking coal deposits are situated here. It is mainly spread across the Chota Nagpur plateau, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and West Bengal.
                                                                                                                                        • Total coal production of Chhattisgarh in 2024-25 was 204.953 Million tonnes and total storage (1st April, 2023) is 85.26 Billion tonnes.
                                                                                                                                        • Korba coalfield is situated in the Hasdev river basin in Chhattisgarh.

                                                                                                                                        Korba coalfield is an important coalfield of Chhattisgarh.

                                                                                                                                        • Coal reserves of Chhattisgarh are found in Tatapani Ramkola, Bisrampur, Sonhat, Jhilimili, Chirimiri, Lakhanpur, Panchbahini and Sendurgarh etc.
                                                                                                                                        • Talcher is a major coalfield of Odisha situated in the valley of the Brahmani River in Angul district. Talcher coalfield is managed by Mahanadi coalfield Limited which is a subsidiary of Coal India Limited.
                                                                                                                                        • Raniganj is a coalfield of West Bengal. Coalfields of West Bengal are Barjora, Birbhum and Darjeeling.
                                                                                                                                        • Namchik- Namphuk and Miao Bum coalfields are situated in Arunachal Pradesh.
                                                                                                                                        • Coalbed methane and shale gas are unconventional sources of energy. Coalbed methane is 90% more pure methane gas extracted from the coal seam. Shale gas is extracted from fine-grained sedimentary rocks.
                                                                                                                                        • Shale gas is not only a mixture of propane and butane but it also contains more than 90% methane, 4% ethene, 1% propane and various other gases. Huge reserves of shale gas are found in the Sindhu-Gangetic region, Assam, Gujarat, Rajasthan and the coastal region. Currently, coal industry in India is facing a lot of challenges. Some of them are low quality coal, deficiencies in coal washing establishment, higher imports of coking coal, etc.
                                                                                                                                        • Where was first coal mine in India mined?Raniganj

                                                                                                                                        India's first coal mine → Raniganj, on the Damodar river, mined from 1774.

                                                                                                                                              Energy Mineral · Petroleum and Natural Gas: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                              • Petroleum or mineral oil is the next major energy source in India after coal.
                                                                                                                                              • It provides fuel for heat and lighting, lubricants for machinery and raw materials for a number of manufacturing industries.
                                                                                                                                              • Petroleum refineries act as a nodal industry for synthetic textiles, fertilizers and numerous chemical industries.
                                                                                                                                              • It is found in anticlines and fault traps of tertiary rocks in India.
                                                                                                                                              • At first, petroleum was detected near Margherita by Assam Railway and Trading Company in 1860. Next, in 1867, the first oil well was drilled in Makum (Assam). The oldest oil deposits in India are in Digboi (Assam). It is situated in the Brahmaputra Valley.
                                                                                                                                              • The four main regions of crude mineral oil are –

                                                                                                                                              (1) Brahmaputra Valley

                                                                                                                                              (2) Gujarat Coast

                                                                                                                                              (3) Western Coast

                                                                                                                                              (4) Eastern Coast

                                                                                                                                              Map not to scale

                                                                                                                                              Brahmaputra Valley (Upper Assam Basin) is India's oldest oil producing region,with the first commercially successful oil discovery at Digboi in 1889 and the main producing belt lies in Upper Assam, largely along/near the Noa Dihing and Dihing (Burhi Dihing) river valleys - mainly in today's Tinsukia and Dibrugarh districts and adjoining parts of the Sivasagar belt. Major oil producing centers are Nahar Katiya, Digboi, Hugri Jan-Moran, Rudra Sagar, Lakwa and Surmaghati. Nuna Mati oil refining plant is situated in Assam. It comes under the authority of Indian Oil Corporation. It was established in 1962 near Guwahati.

                                                                                                                                              • Similarly, Digboi and Numaligarh oil refineries are situated in Assam. Gujarat is placed at first in crude oil production in India during 2024-25 P (as per Annual Report of Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, 2024-25) and placed at second ifwe include offshore crude oil production.
                                                                                                                                              • Ankleshwar is extendes over about 38.98 km square area of Bharuch district of Gujarat. Here, oil was searched for in 1960 and production started in 1961.
                                                                                                                                              • Lunej oil production region is situated in the upper portions of the Gulf of Khambat in Gujarat.
                                                                                                                                              • Kalol field is situated in Ahmedabad (Gujarat). Its major producing centers include Nawagram, Dholka, Somasan, Kosamba, etc.
                                                                                                                                              • Koyali oil refinery (IOCL) is located in Gujarat.
                                                                                                                                              • The city of Jamnagar was established by Jam Rawal in 1540 in Gujarat. At that time, it was known as Nawanagar. Here the largest refineries in the world have been established by the Reliance Industries. The western offshore region is an important center of oil production in India. Under it, the Bombay High Basin is situated about 160 km from the coast of Mumbai. It wasjointly explored by Russia and India. First oil well was dug up here in 1974.
                                                                                                                                              • Aliabet Mineral Oil Field is included in the western offshore region. This oil field is situated near Aliabet Island in the Cambay Basin, about 45 km away from Bhavnagar.
                                                                                                                                              • the eastern offshore region of oil fields in India includes the deltaic regions of the Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery rivers which are highly associated with mineral oil and natural gas.
                                                                                                                                              • Narimanam and Kovilkalappal offshore regions produces crude oil in the Cauvery Basin. Deposits of crude oil have been found in the Rajasthan Desert, Bilaspur Tehsil of Rampur district (U.P.) and Jwalamukhi region of Punjab.
                                                                                                                                              • Maugalbhagyam, Shakti and Aishwarya are prominent oil-fields identified in the Barmer Sanchore basin near Barmer in Rajasthan.
                                                                                                                                              • Oil deposits in the offshore region of India is mainly controlled by the central government.
                                                                                                                                              • Most of the crude oil produced in India are from this region only.

                                                                                                                                              Bombay High, which lies in the offshore region, is the largest petroleum-producing region.

                                                                                                                                              • The first terrible energy crisis occurred in India, in 1973 when oil-exporting countries had increased the oil prices by more than 4 times.
                                                                                                                                              • According to the Annual Report 2024-25 (Ministry of Petrolieum and Natural Gas), major production 2024-25 (P) of natural gas in India is carried out from the offshore region of the Bombay High Basin.

                                                                                                                                              Leading natural gas producers are

                                                                                                                                              The production of natural gas was 36106 MMSCM in 2024- 25 (P). Offshore areas continued to be the largest producer of natural gas (utilised) with a share of 71.81%, followed by Assam (9.83%), Rajasthan (4.95%), Tripura (3.39%), Gujarat (2.91%), Tamil Nadu (2.81%) and the remaining

                                                                                                                                              4.3% of the total production was contributed together by Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Jharkhand (CBM), Madhya Pradesh (CBM) and West Bengal (CBM).

                                                                                                                                              • Hazira - Vijaipur - Jagdishpur (HVJ) gas pipeline has been constructed by Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL) to transport gas.
                                                                                                                                              • Oil exploration and production in India is undertaken by Oil India Limited and ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited).
                                                                                                                                              • Oil transportation and distribution is supervised by Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL).
                                                                                                                                              • The largest deposits of Natural gas are found in the Bombay High Basin. Besides this Naharkatiya, Moran Region (Assam), Jagatiya, Godha (Gujarat), Mangamdam, Awadi, Virugambakkam (Tamil Nadu) Namchick and Miyao-Pung (Arunachal Pradesh) etc. also have reserves of oil and natural gas resources.
                                                                                                                                              • Reliance Industries Limited searched the abundant stock of natural gas in 2002-2003 in the Cauvery-Godavari-6 Basin in offshore region of Andhra Pradesh. Reliance is the first private company in India that is exploring natural gas at depths about 6000 meters below the ocean surface in the offshore region.
                                                                                                                                              • According to Hydrocarbon DG (Directorate General), ONGC has estimated 187.5 TCF gas reserves in 5 basins.

                                                                                                                                                    Energy Mineral · Miscellaneous : Minerals: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                    • Minerals are generally found in the earth's crust in ore form. Several types of the minerals are found in a different regions of India, but these are unequally distributed.
                                                                                                                                                    • Earlier, India was first in mica production. Mica was declared a minor mineral on 10 Feb, 2015, but it was classified as a major mineral after Gazette Notification S.O. 924 (E) dated 20 February, 2025. In this notification also included three other minerals (Barytes, Felspar and Quartz), which were shifted from minor to major categories. The minor minerals are Barytes (Major), Bentonite, Calcite, Corundum (Minor) & Sapphire (Major), Diaspore, Dolomite, Dunite & Pyroxenite, Feldespar (Major), Fireclay, Fuller's Earth, Granite, Gypsum (Minor) & Selenite (Major), Kaolin, Ball Clay, Other Clay & Shale, Laterite, Marble, Mica, Ochre, Other Calcareous Materials, Pyrophyllite, Quartz (Major) & Other Silica Minerals [Moulding Sand and Flint Stone (Major)], Slate, Sandstone & Other Dimension Stones, Talc, Soapstone and Steatite.
                                                                                                                                                    • The only producer of asbestos as per the data of the year 2013-14 is Andhra Pradesh, whereas its largest reserves/ resources (as on April 1, 2020) are found in Rajasthan. No production of asbestos was reported in 2023-24 as well as in the previous year and no reporting mines were noted in 2023-24 as well as in the preceding year.
                                                                                                                                                    • Metamorphic rock is a result of the transformation of existing rock, in a process called metamorphism.
                                                                                                                                                    • Metamorphic minerals are formed under high temperature and pressure. Garnet is associated with metamorphism.

                                                                                                                                                    Five leading states in manganese ore production as per the figures of the year, 2023-24 (P) are

                                                                                                                                                    1. Madhya Pradesh 1033424 tonnes

                                                                                                                                                    2. Maharashtra 1032992 tonnes

                                                                                                                                                    3. Odisha 650856 tonnes

                                                                                                                                                    4. Karnataka 355057 tonnes

                                                                                                                                                    5. Andhra Pradesh 297537 tonnes

                                                                                                                                                    • Manganese is mainly found in Balaghat and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh and, Bhandara and Nagpur districts of Maharashtra. Manganese extracted from Odisha is rich in iron content and lacks in phosphorus. Balaghat is an important district of Madhya Pradesh in the perspective of mineral resources. The major minerals found here are kyanite, manganese ore, copper etc.
                                                                                                                                                    • Nickel is a lustrous, silvery-white metal. It is the fifth most common element in the Earth's crust. Nickel does not occur in a native state. The largest resources (as on April 1, 2020) of nickel in India are present in Odisha, but it is not mined. The entire demand for nickel in India is met through imports.
                                                                                                                                                    • Lead mainly occurs in metamorphic rock (schist) in a combined form with silver. It is also found in Precambrian and Vindhyan limestone. Lead is resistant with respect to acidic matter and atmospheric corrosion.
                                                                                                                                                    • According to data from the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2024, Rajasthan is the only producer of lead in India. The Zawar region is famous for lead production.
                                                                                                                                                    • Gypsum is found in large quantities in Churu-Bikaner-Sri Ganganagar belt. It is used for improving soil fertility. It is also used in the health and construction sectors after value addition.
                                                                                                                                                    • Rajasthan is the largest (2021-22) producer of Gypsum.
                                                                                                                                                    • Jaduguda Mine in eastern Singhbhum district of Jharkhand is famous for uranium production. Other uranium production regions are Domiasiat (Meghalaya), Lambapur (Andhra Pradesh), Rohail (Rajasthan) and Gogi (Karnataka). In Uttar Pradesh, uranium is found in Lalitpur. Monazite is an important ore of thorium, lanthanum, uranium and cerium. It is found in large quantities in the coastal areas of Kerala.
                                                                                                                                                    • Large reserves of diamond bearing kimberlite tracts have been discovered in Payalikhand and Behradih in Gariaband district of Chhattisgarh.

                                                                                                                                                          Electrical Energy · Thermal: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                          • Vital energy like coal, crude oil and natural gas are used to produce thermal electrical energy in India. The National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) was established in 1975. As per the Ministry of Power, the installed power capacity in India as of December 31, 2025 was 513729.69 MW. In this, thermal energy has the highest share of 48.07%

                                                                                                                                                          i.e. 246941.62 MW. Coal contributes 219610.00 MW, lignite 6620.00 MW, gas 20122.42 MW and diesel 589.20 MW to thermal power installed capacity. The share of other sectors in the total power generation of India is: hydropower 50914.66 MW, nuclear power 8780.00 MW, and non conventional energy (renewable energy) 207093.41 MW.

                                                                                                                                                          • Government of India is going to start an Ultra Mega Power Project based on coal with Power Finance Corporation as its nodal agency. Usage of super critical technique is proposed in this project to cut the carbon emissions. Each of these Ultra Mega Power Projects has a capacity of 4,000 MW or above.
                                                                                                                                                          • Tata Power is establishing an Ultra Mega Power Project in Mundra (Gujarat). According to Ministry of Power, initially, following nine (9) numbers Ultra Mega Power Projects (UMPPs) were proposed to be set up in different states:

                                                                                                                                                          (i) Sasan UMPP in Madhya Pradesh - Coal pithead,

                                                                                                                                                          (ii) Mundra UMPP in Gujarat - Coastal,

                                                                                                                                                          (iii) Krishnapatnam UMPP in Andhra Pradesh - Coastal,

                                                                                                                                                          (iv) Tilaiya UMPP in Jharkhand - Coal pithead

                                                                                                                                                          (v) Akaltara UMPP in Chhattisgarh - Coal pithead,

                                                                                                                                                          (vi) Bedabahal UMPP in Odisha - Coal pithead,

                                                                                                                                                          (vii) Cheyyur UMPP in Tamil Nadu - Domestic coal based,

                                                                                                                                                          (viii) Girye UMPP in Maharashtra - Coastal,

                                                                                                                                                          (ix) Tadri UMPP in Karnataka - Coastal.

                                                                                                                                                          In addition to nine UMPPs originally identified a request has come from some of the state governments for installation of additional UMPPs in their states. These are given below-

                                                                                                                                                          (i) Two additional UMPPs in Odisha

                                                                                                                                                          (ii) 2nd UMPP in Gujarat

                                                                                                                                                          (iii) 2nd UMPP in Jharkhand - Deoghar UMPP

                                                                                                                                                          (iv) 2nd UMPP in Tamil Nadu

                                                                                                                                                          (v) UMPP in Bihar - Banka UMPP

                                                                                                                                                          (vi) UMPP in Uttar Pradesh

                                                                                                                                                          (vii) 2nd UMPP in Andhra Pradesh.

                                                                                                                                                          • Neyveli Thermal Power Corporation in Tamil Nadu is the first plant of South Asia working on lignite coal. Lignite is a tertiary category of coal.
                                                                                                                                                          • NTPC Farakka Thermal Power Plant is situated in Murshidabad district of West Bengal. It gets water from Farakka feeder canal and coal from Rajmahal coalfield. Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station is situated in Telangana. Its total capacity is 2600 MW.
                                                                                                                                                          • Obra Thermal Power Station was established in 1967 with the help of Russian engineers in Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh.
                                                                                                                                                          • Bokaro Thermal Power Plant is situated in Jharkhand.

                                                                                                                                                          MMaapp nnoott ttooscsaclaele

                                                                                                                                                          • Major Thermal Power Plants of India include: Ukai Thermal Power Corporation (Gujarat), Patratu Thermal Power Plant (Jharkhand), Dabhol Thermal Power Plant (Maharashtra), Utran Thermal Power Plant (Gujarat), Raichur (Karnataka), etc. Kothagudem Thermal Power Plants situated in Telangana. Uran Gas Turbine Power Station is a gas based power project situated in Raigad district of Maharashtra. It is operated by Maharashtra State Power Generation Company Limited.
                                                                                                                                                          Electrical Energy · Nuclear Energy: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                          • The most promising source of energy to fulfill the future demand for energy in India is nuclear energy. India’s first Nuclear Power Reactor was established at Tarapur in 1969. Tarapur Atomic Power Station was constructed initially with a boiling water reactor (BWR) that was based on American technology.
                                                                                                                                                          • Production of nuclear energy requires uranium thorium and heavy water.
                                                                                                                                                          • Uranium is the most widely used mineral in Atomic Power Station as a fuel.
                                                                                                                                                          • A total of around 513729.69 MW of energy capacity has been installed in the country as of31 December, 2025 which includes 8780 MW from nuclear energy which is 1.71% of the total installed energy capacity.
                                                                                                                                                          • Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station was established in 1973 with the cooperation of Canada in Kota.

                                                                                                                                                          Map not to scale

                                                                                                                                                          • Narora Atomic Power Station is located in Narora, Bulandshahar District in Uttar Pradesh.
                                                                                                                                                          • Kakrapar Atomic Power Station is located in Surat District of Gujarat.
                                                                                                                                                          • In 1988, Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant was established with the cooperation of Russia (the then Soviet Union) in Kudankulam, Tirunelveli District of Tamil Nadu through an agreement. Under this agreement, Russia has been building two nuclear reactors for India since 2002. Under the Intergovernmental Agreement in December 2008, Russia agreed to supply four more nuclear reactors to India. All four reactors are in the implementation phase.
                                                                                                                                                          • Kaiga Generating Station is a nuclear power generating station situated at Kaiga, near the river Kali, in Karnataka. It has four units.
                                                                                                                                                          • The First Reactor of the Kundankulam nuclear power plant, which is located in Kundankulam area (district- Tirunelveli), of Tamil Nadu, is a pressurized water reactor.
                                                                                                                                                          • Mithivirdi Nuclear Power Station was established with the cooperation of the U.S.A. The project is a part of the Indo-U.S. nuclear deal signed in 2008. In 2015, the 6000 MW project was approved by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change for the coastal regulatory area. This nuclear power plant is located in the Bhavnagar district of Gujarat.
                                                                                                                                                          • The Jaitapur Nuclear Power Project in India was originally associated with AREVA of France, but the French reactor business is now represented by EDF. The project is proposed at Jaitapur in Ratnagiri district, Maharashtra.

                                                                                                                                                          For the nuclear energy, a heavy water plant is required.

                                                                                                                                                          • Thal Heavy Water Plant is located in Maharashtra.
                                                                                                                                                          • Manuguru Heavy Water Plant is located in Telangana.
                                                                                                                                                          • There are seven heavy water plants in the country. These are Vadodara (Gujarat), Hazira (Gujarat), Kota (Rajasthan), Thal (Maharashtra), Manuguru (Telangana), Talcher (Odisha) and Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu).
                                                                                                                                                          • Nuclear Power Corporation Limited is the joint venture of NTPC and NPCIL.
                                                                                                                                                          • NPCIL has a 51% stake in Nuclear Power Corporation Limited and 49% of NTPC. It was established in January 2011.
                                                                                                                                                          Electrical Energy · Hydroelectricity: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                          • Hydroelectricity in India is one of the major sources of energy. Hydroelectricity is generated by fast flowing water, which is a renewable resource. It is easiest to develop hydroelectricity in mountainous areas. The first small hydro project of 130 kW. commissioned in the hills of Darjeeling in 1897 marked the development of hydropower in India. The Shivasamudram project of 4500 kW was the next to come up in the Mandya district of Karnataka in 1902, for the supply of power to the Kolar Gold Mines. Now India has a number of multi-purpose projects like the Bhakra Nangal and Damodar Valley Project etc. producing hydroelectric power. National Hydroelectric Power Corporation (NHPC) Limited is the largest hydropower development organization in India, with capabilities to undertake all the activities from conceptualization to commissioning of hydro projects. NHPC has also diversified in the field of solar and wind energy development etc.

                                                                                                                                                          NHPC Ltd. was incorporated in 1975 under the Companies Act, 1956. The company is mandated to plan, promote and organize an integrated and efficient development of power in all its aspects through conventional and non-conventional sources in India and abroad. NHPC is a listed company on the NSE and BSE, successfully concluding its IPO in 2009. NHPC Power Station Under Operation (Incl. JV)

                                                                                                                                                          Electrical Energy · Energy : Miscellaneous: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                          • Sources of energy that appear in the form of coal, petroleum, natural gas and nuclear energy are commercial resources. Fossil Fuels such as coal, Petroleum and Natural Gas are conventional sources of energy and are non-renew able resources. In contrast, solars and wind energy, biogas, biomass/energy from agricultural residues, geothermal energy, tidal energy, and small hydropower are non-conventional (renewable) source of energy. Renewable (new) energy resources are those that are naturally replenished or restored by natural/cyclical processes within a reasonably short period of time.
                                                                                                                                                          • The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy gave approval to the Consolidated Energy Policy on 26 December, 2008.
                                                                                                                                                          • Solar energy is a huge resource of non-exhaustible form of energy. It is used for cooking, water purification, electricity generation, etc. India receives approximately 5 kW per cm² of solar radiation energy for nearly 300 days in a year.
                                                                                                                                                          • Rampura village (Jhansi district) is the first village in India that has installed its own Solar Energy Plant and is situated in Uttar Pradesh. The first solar photovoltaic plant of 2MW capacity in India is installed in Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal near Asansol. Maharashtra is famous for the Satara Wind Energy Plant. The suitable states for the production of wind energy in India are Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana and Rajasthan, etc.
                                                                                                                                                          • According to the figures of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy the assessment indicates a gross power potential of 695.50 GW and 1163.9 GW in the country at 120 meter and 150 meters respectively, above ground level. The installed capacity of grid-interactive wind power in the country as on December 31, 2025 is 54.51 GW.
                                                                                                                                                          • According to the figures of the Ministry of New and Renew able Energy as of December 31, 2025, Gujarat (14820.94 MW) stands first the wind power installed capacity. followed by Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Maharashtra.

                                                                                                                                                          • Electrical energy produced due to high and low tides in the sea is known as tidal energy. In India there are two major areas for Tidal Energy:

                                                                                                                                                          1. Rann of Kutch and GulfofKhambhat (previously known as Gulf of Cambay) i.e. the Gujarat coastal area. The maximum tidal range is 8-11 m, whereas the average tidal range is 6.77 m-5.23 m. There is a tidal range of height 5 m approximately, whereas the average tidal range is 2.97 m.

                                                                                                                                                          2. Sundarban delta in West Bengal. India’s first geothermal Electric Plant was installed in Khammam in Andhra Pradesh (now Telangana) in 2012. The geothermal energy based Manikaran Electrical Plant is situated in Kullu, Himachal Pradesh. It is famous for its hot water sources. Electricity produced from hot water sources is generated in the mountain valleys of Manikaran. Hot water sources are also found in Kasol, Kheer Ganga and Pulga in addition to Manikaran.

                                                                                                                                                          Industry: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                          i. Iron and Steel Industry

                                                                                                                                                          • The iron and steel industry is a basic industry. The first attempt to make iron in India started in 1830 A.D. in Porto Novo (Tamil Nadu), but this factory late failed. For the first time in India, iron was successfully produced by the Bengal Ironworks in Kulti in 1875 AD. In the year 1907, a new factory was established in India by the Tata Iron and Steel Company at Sakchi (Jamshedpur). Where raw iron was produced in the year 1908 and steel was produced in the year 1912. According to World Steel Association data (World Steel in figures), 2025, it is the world’s 10th largest (in the year, 2024) steel company (Tata in Steel Group, 2024) with an annual production capacity of 31.02 million tonnes. Map not to scale
                                                                                                                                                          • Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Ltd. (VISL) was established in the year 1923 on the bank of the Bhadravati River in Shivamogga District of Karnataka. Iron Ore is supplied from the Bababudan Hills, while limestone is sourced from Bhandigunda. Due to the lack of local supply of coal supply, charcoal or wood was used for power which was sourced from the Malnad forest area. Since 1989, it has acted as a subsidiary of the Steel Authority of India Ltd. It was completely merged with SAIL in the year 1998.
                                                                                                                                                          • After the independence, during the second five-year plan of India, special emphasis was given to heavy and basic industries under which Rourkela (Odisha), Bhilai (Chhattisgarh), and Durgapur (West Bengal) steel plants were established.
                                                                                                                                                          • Rourkela Steel Plant (RSP), originally set up under Hindustan Steel Limited (HSL) and now a unit of SAIL is located at Rourkela in Sundargarh district of Odisha. This factory was established in collaboration with Germany’s companies Krupp and Demag. It is situated near deposits of manganese and limestone. Iron ore is brought from Odisha's Keonjhar district. Coking Coal is sourced mainly from the Jharia and Bokaro Coalfield (including the Kargali/CCL washery area in Bokaro, Jharkhand), while Talcher coalfield (Odisha) is largely known for non-coking thermal Coal.
                                                                                                                                                          • Limestone and dolomite are obtained from Birmitrapur. It gets cheap hydroelectricity from Hirakud easily.
                                                                                                                                                          • The Bhilai steel plant was established with the help of the former Soviet Union in Bhilai of Durg District in the state of Chhattisgarh on the Kolkata-Mumbai railroad. The Dalli Rajhara iron ore deposit supplies iron ore to the Bhilai steel plant.
                                                                                                                                                          • Hindustan Steel Limited (HSL)-Durgapur- the Durgapur steel plant was established with the collaboration of Britain near Asansol in the Paschim Bardhaman district of West Bengal. This plant obtains iron ore from the Bolani mines of the Gua area, Coal from the mines of Barakar and Jharia, manganese from Jamda (Keonjhar District) and electricity and water from the Damodar River.
                                                                                                                                                          • Bokaro Steel Limited (BSL) - Bokaro -This plant was established with the collaboration of the then Soviet Union at the confluence of the Bokaro and Damodar rivers in the Bokaro district of the state of Jharkhand.
                                                                                                                                                          • Major minerals required for the iron and steel industry are iron ore, coking coal, manganese, rock phosphate, dolomite and chromium etc. Due to a lack of coking coal in the country, it is imported from Australia.
                                                                                                                                                          • Generally chromium and nickel are used in the making of stainless steel. Both of these are mixed with iron metal along with some quantity of carbon for the manufacturing of stainless-steel.
                                                                                                                                                          • The Visakhapatnam steel plant is India’s first steel plant located on a coastline steel plant. Iron ore is supplied to this plant from Bailadila (Chhattisgarh).
                                                                                                                                                          Industry · Aluminium Industry: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                          • The aluminium industry in India was registered in the year 1937 and started producing alumina in 1942, with the establishment of ‘Aluminium Corporation of India’ in J.K. Nagar (West Bengal).
                                                                                                                                                          • In India, two new aluminium plants Hirakud (INDAL) and Renukoot (Hindalco), the were set up during the second five-year plan. HINDALCO is a company of Aditya Birla Group. It was established in the year 1958 producing copper and aluminium.
                                                                                                                                                          • In the year 1962, the aluminium production plant of this company was established in Renukoot (Sonbhadra) in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Novelis Inc. was acquired by HINDALCO in May 2007.
                                                                                                                                                          • Bharat Aluminium Company Limited (BALCO) was incorporated in Korba in the year 1965. Bauxite is supplied to this plant from Amarkantak (Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh) and Gandhamardan (Odisha) and electricity is supplied from the Korba thermal powerhouse.
                                                                                                                                                          • BALCO is the first Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) in producing aluminium.

                                                                                                                                                          Map not to scale

                                                                                                                                                          • Indian Aluminium Company Ltd. (INDAL) started working as a public sector company in the year 1944. It has two aluminium units. The first is established in Hirakund (Odisha) and the second in Alupuram (Kerala).
                                                                                                                                                          • National Aluminium Company (NALCO) was established in 1981 haMvainpgnoitttsorsecgaliestered office at Bhubaneshwar. Significantly, the company has been operating its captive Panchpatmali. Bauxite Mines for the pithead alumina refinery at Damanjodi, in the district of Koraput in Odisha.

                                                                                                                                                          It is now an 'A' Navratna CPSE. It is one of Asia’s largest integrated aluminium institutes.

                                                                                                                                                          • Hindustan Copper Limited is located in Khetri, Rajasthan, which is the only company that originally produces copper in the country.

                                                                                                                                                                Industry · Miscellaneous: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                • Cement industry mainly depends on limestone. Due to this, the cement industry is mainly located in the areas having an abundance of limestone.
                                                                                                                                                                • According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2022 India stands second in cement production at the global level, after China. The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, government of India, publishes data on production and capacity of cement in its Annual Reports. As per The Annual Report 2024-25, the total installed capacity of cement plants has been placed at 640 million tonnes. During 2023-24, the production of cement was 426.29 million tonnes which showed an increase of 8.91% as compared to the year 2022-23, which reported a production of 391.40 million tonnes.

                                                                                                                                                                Map not to scale

                                                                                                                                                                • Chunar is renowned for its cement industry. Apart from it, cement factories like Dadri (Gautam Buddha Nagar), Churk (Sonbhadra) and Dalla (Sonbhadra) are located in Uttar Pradesh.
                                                                                                                                                                • Uttar Pradesh is also famous for the glass industry. Bahjoi, Naini, Firozabad, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Lucknow, Makhanpur, Hiranpur, Varanasi and Sasni etc. are major centres of the glass industry.
                                                                                                                                                                • Firozabad, in the state of Uttar Pradesh is also known as the 'City of Bangles'.
                                                                                                                                                                • Dalmianagar is one of the oldest and biggest industrial towns in India.
                                                                                                                                                                • It is situated on the bank of the Son River in Rohtas district of Bihar.
                                                                                                                                                                • It is famous for its cement industry.
                                                                                                                                                                • It was founded by Ram Krishna Dalmiya of the Dalmiya Group of Industries.
                                                                                                                                                                • The first Indian cotton cloth mill was established in 1818 at Fort Gloster near Kolkata, although this mill was a failure. The second cotton mill in India was established by KGN Daber in 1854 (in Mumbai) and was named the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company. It is considered the true foundation of the modern cotton industry in India.
                                                                                                                                                                • In India, cotton is mainly produced in black soils. Some of the important centers, such as Ahmedabad, Solapur, Nagpur, Coimbatore and Indore are located in the areas of large scale cotton cultivation. Thus, cotton is produced in only a few regions of India. It is equally important to note that cotton is a pure raw material, in the sense that it does not lose its weight in the process of manufacturing and the slight loss in weight is more than compensated by the use ofsizing materials. The cotton textile industry is spread all over India. Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, Punjab and Madhya Pradesh etc. are prime centers of cotton textiles.
                                                                                                                                                                • Tamil Nadu is a leading producer of mill-made cotton yarn in the country. The presence of numerous spinning mills, a skilled labor force, and the availability, of cheap hydroelectricity are the main factors for good production.
                                                                                                                                                                • Ludhiana in Punjab is famous for the hosiery industry. It is renowned as the industrial capital of Punjab. It is known for ready-made garments, hosiery items, sewing machines and parts and machine tools.

                                                                                                                                                                The then Prime Minister Jawahar lal Nehru formally inaugurated the Ammonium Sulphate factory in Sindri (then Bihar now Jharkhand) on 2nd March, 1952. After that, the fertilizer plant was established in Nangal (Punjab).

                                                                                                                                                                Phulpur (Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh) has the largest co operative fertilizer factory. The Phulpur unit of IFFCO (Indian Farmers Fertiliser Co-operative Limited) was established in 1974, with the laying of the foundation stone by the then Prime Minister of India Mrs. Indira Gandhi. The other units of IFFCO are at Kalol, Kandla,Aonla and Paradeep.

                                                                                                                                                                • Heavy Engineering Corporation Ltd. is one of the leading suppliers of capital equipment in India for steel, mining, railways, power, defense, space research, nuclear and strategic sectors. set-up in the year 1958 in Ranchi, HEC has acquired expertise in its field through its more than half a century of experience.
                                                                                                                                                                • Hindustan Machine Tools Limited, formerly Indian Tool, is a state-owned manufacturing company incorporated as "Hindustan Machine Tools" as Bengaluru in 1953. It is a Central Public Sector Enterprise of the Government of India, under the Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industries. The company manufactures tractors and watches under its watch division as well as industrial machines and tools mainly under its Praga division. It has manufacturing unit locations in Bangalore, Pinjore, Kalamassery, Hyderabad and Ajmer.
                                                                                                                                                                • Hindustan Aluminium Company Ltd (HINDALCO), a metal flagship company of the Aditya Birla Group, is located in Pipari village (Renukoot) in the Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh.
                                                                                                                                                                • Fertilizer Corporation of India Limited is a Public Sector Undertaking in India under the administrative control of the Department of Fertilizers, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers. The company was incorporated in 1961 and FCIL was reorganized in 1978. FCIL has manufacturing units in five states: namely Sindri complex (Jharkhand), Gorakhpur complex (Uttar Pradesh), Ramagundam complex (Telangana), Talcher complex (Odisha) and an uncommissioned project in Korba (Chhattisgarh).
                                                                                                                                                                • The Diesel Locomotive Works (DLW) (now known as 'Banaras Locomotive Works') is located in Varanasi and was founded in 1961. The DLW is a production unit owned by Indian Railways, that manufactures diesel-electric locomotives and their spare parts.
                                                                                                                                                                • Indian Telephone Industries Limited, commonly known as ITI Limited, is a state-owned manufacturer of telecommunication equipment in India. It was founded in 1948 and has six manufacturing units in Bengaluru (Karnataka), Naini, Mankapur, Raebareli (Uttar Pradesh), Palakkad (Kerala) and Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir), which produce a range of switching, transmission, access and subscriber premises equipment. Its headquarters is in Bangalore.
                                                                                                                                                                • Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) was incorporated in 1954. The manufacturing units of Bharat Electronics Limited are located in the following cities of India - Bengaluru, Chennai (Tamil Nadu), Panchkula (Haryana), Kotdwara (Uttarakhand), Ghaziabad (Uttar Pradesh), Pune, Hyderabad (Telangana) and Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh).

                                                                                                                                                                The Mathura Refinery, owned by Indian Oil Corporation, is located in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.

                                                                                                                                                                • The shipyard factory was established at Visakhapatnam in 1941 and was taken over by the government in 1952 was renamed Hindustan Shipyard Ltd. Apart from Vishakhapatnam, there are four main centers of the shipbuilding industry in Goa, Kolkata, Kochi and Mumbai in India; all are public sector undertakings.
                                                                                                                                                                • The alumina plants are located in Damanjodi (Odisha), Korba (Chhattisgarh), Renukoot (Uttar Pradesh), Metur (Tamil Nadu), Muri (Jharkhand) and Belgaum (Karnataka). At present, most of the India's vehicles are manufactured in India. The premier units related to this industry are Hindustan Motors (Kolkata), Premier Automobile Limited (Mumbai), Ashok (Leyland) (Chennai), Tata Engineering Company Limited (Jamshedpur), Mahindra & Mahindra (Pune), Maruti Industries Limited (Gurugram) and Sunrise Industries (Bengaluru).
                                                                                                                                                                • Currently only, nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers are produced in India. Panki is a significant place for the fertilizer industry.
                                                                                                                                                                • The largest petrochemical factory is located in Jamnagar, the state of Gujarat in India.

                                                                                                                                                                (1) Petronet LNG Ltd. is an Indian oil and gas company formed by the government of India to import liquefied natural gas (LNG) and set up LNG terminals in the country. It is a joint venture company promoted by the Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL), Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) with an authorized capital. Petronet LNG Ltd has set up its first LNG terminal at Dahej in Gujarat with a capacity of 17.5 million metric tonnes per year. Another terminal with a capacity of 5 million tonnes per year was commissioned in Kochi (Kerala). The earlier proposed to develop Petronet LNG's LNG terminal at Gangavaram Port (Andhra Pradesh) did not progress and Petronet LNG is now pursuing a 5 MMTPA land based (greenfield) LNG regasification terminal at Gopalpur Port, Ganjam (Odisha).
