                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Universe · The Asteroids: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The group of small pieces of rock and metal revolving around the Sun between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter is called asteroids.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Asteroids, vary in size and some can be 1000 km in diameter for example Ceres.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to the position of these asteroids in space, they are categorized in the following way –

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (i) Main belt - In this belt, there are some prominent asteroids named Hungaria, Flora, Phocaea, Eos, Themis, Cybele, Hilda and Koronis.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (ii) Near Earth Asteroids (NEAs) - Among these Aten, Apollo, Amor and Atira are prominent ones.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (iii) Trojans - Near the Lagrange point of the planet Jupiter orbit.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Universe · The Comets and Meteors: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A comet is an icy, small solar system body that, when pass ing close to the sun, warms and begins to release gases. This produces a visible atmosphere or coma and sometimes also a tail. Comets usually have highly elliptical orbits and they revolve around the sun. Sometimes the tail of these comets can be millions of kilometers long.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Comets generally have two kinds of tails – (1) comprised of dust particles and (2) ionized. Both are generated from the Coma.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Sun's radiation pressure and solar wind accelerate materials away from the comet’s head at different velocities according to the size and mass of the materials.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Halley's Comet was last seen in Earth's skies in 1986 and will return in 2061 on its regular 76 year journey around the Sun. The Halley is a short period comet. On 23rd July 1995, the Hale-Bopp comet was first seen near Jupiter. It was discovered by Alan Hale (New Mexico) and Thomas Bopp (Arizona). The last names of these two people were combined to name this comet. The Hale-Bopp is a long period comet which takes 2534 years to revolve around the Sun.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Hale-Bopp comet is 1000 times brighter than the Halley comet, even though they are at the same distances. The comet Shoemaker Levy-9 was discovered on 24th March, 1993 by astronomers Eugene M. Shoemaker, Carolyn Shoemaker and David Levy. The last names of both the astronomers were used to name the comet. Between 16 and 22 July 1994, the comet collided with Jupiter, providing the first direct observation of an extraterrestrial collision of solar system objects. However, Jupiter was not harmed by this collision.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • 67 P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko was the destination of the Rosetta mission launched on 2nd March 2004. It was the first mission to land a spacecraft on a comet. It was launched from the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana on an Ariane 5G+ rocket and reached comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko on 6 August 2014.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Earth: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                                                                          i. Latitudes

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Latitude is the angular distance of a point on the earth’s surface, measured in degrees from the center of the earth.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • It is parallel to the line of the equator, which lies midway between the poles.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The latitude angle is denoted by the Greek lowercase letter Phi (). 0° latitude is also known as the equator. It is halfway between the North Pole and the South Pole. The equator thus divides the planet into the Northern and Southern hemisphere.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The earth is widest at the equator. All other latitudes are smaller than the equator.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The North Pole has a latitude of 90°N and the South Pole has a latitude of 90°S. In each hemisphere, latitudes are counted from 0° to the poles. Hence, altogether there are 179 latitudes (including the equator). Besides this, there are 179 real circle latitudes as the 90° N and 90°S latitudes are points on the earth’s surface.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The 23.5° N latitude in the Northern Hemisphere is known as the Tropic of Cancer whereas the 66.5° N latitude in the Northern Hemisphere is known as Arctic Circle.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Similarly, the 23.5°S latitude in the southern Hemisphere is known as the Tropic of Capricorn and 66.5° south latitude in the Southern Hemisphere is known as the Antarctic Circle.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The 0° latitude (equator) and 0° longitude (Prime Meridian) intersect each other in the Gulf of Guinea located on the western coast of Africa. The Gulf is located in the Atlantic Ocean. The north and south of any place on a globe or a map is determined by latitudes. The latitudinal value in degrees of any place is directly proportional to its extent in the north of the equator for example - Beijing (China) - 39°55'N, New Delhi - 28°38'N, New York (USA) - 40°45' N and Rome (Italy) - 41°54' N. Hence among these Rome is the most northern city.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Earth · The Longitude: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Longitudes are imaginary lines joining the North and South Poles. They are also known as Meridians of Longitude or Lines of Longitude.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • By convention, one of the longitudes was called the Prime Meridian. The longitudes of other places are measured as the angle east or west from the Prime Meridian, ranging from 0° at the Prime Meridian, to 180° eastward and 180° westward. In 1884, at the International Meridian Conference in Washington, D.C., 22 countries voted to adopt the Greenwich meridian as the Prime Meridian of the world. The 180th Meridian or Antemeridian is the meridian 180° both east and west of the Prime Meridian. Thus, it is common to both east longitude and west longitude. Hence there are 360 longitudes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Since Earth makes one complete rotation of 360° in one day or 24 hours, it passes through 15° in one hour or 1° in 4 minutes. The Earth rotates from west to east, so every 15° we go eastward local time is advanced by 1 hour.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The International Date Line, established in 1884 passes through the Mid-Pacific Ocean and roughly follows a 180° longitude North-South line on the Earth. It is located halfway around the world from the prime meridian.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • When we cross the International Date Line from west to east, there is a decrease of one day and if you cross the line from east to west there is a gain of an extra day. This is because there is a difference of 24 hours between 180°E and 180°W longitude. 180°E and 180°W longitude are the same and written as only 180°.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The time at 180°E is 12 hours ahead and at 180° W it is 12 hours behind Greenwich time. A time zone is a region or area that observes the same standard time. The 360 longitudes have been divided into 24 time zones. The world is divided longitudinally into time zones, with each hour difference roughly 15° apart. This means that every time zone has a difference of 1 hour and every longitude has a difference of 4 minutes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The international standard time is determined by the prime meridian.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In the Northern Hemisphere the Prime Meridian passes through the United Kingdom, France and Spain in Europe and Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Togo and Ghana in Africa. The only landmass crossed by the Meridian in the Southern Hemisphere is Antarctica.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Apart from the United Kingdom there are a few more countries that despite being away from GMT (Greenwich Mean Time), use it for determining their standard time. These countries/areas are – Iceland, Ireland, Portugal, Western Sahara, Sao Tome Mauritania, Mali, Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, Ghana, Liberia, Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Gambia, Saint Helena etc. The time difference between Indian Standard Time (82°30' E longitude) and GMT is 5.30 hours.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Katchal, a tiny island near Nicobar Island was virtually unknown untill the Royal Greenwich Laboratory declared that it would be the first inhabited place on Earth to catch the rays of the first sunrise of the millennium. The Katchal island is located at a distance of 1600 km from the mainland of India and 418 km from Port Blair port. The island is located at 7°56' North latitude and 93° 24' East longitude.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • International Date Line (IDL) is an imaginary line of demarcation on the surface of the Earth that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole and demarcates the change of one calendar day to the next.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • IDL is roughly based on the meridian of 180° longitude, roughly down the middle of the Pacific Ocean and halfway around the world from the Greenwich Meridian. The IDL is deviated east or west away from the meridian eight places to prevent any anomalies regarding the date at a particular place.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The difference between the International Date Line (180° longitude) and Indian Standard Time (82°30' East) is 97°30' longitude. International Date Line passes through the Bering Strait (Pacific Ocean).
                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Earth · The Equator: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Latitudes are the angular distance of a point on the earth’s surface, measured in degrees from the center of the earth.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • An equator is the 0° circle of latitude (parallel). It is the imaginary line on the spheroid’s surface, equidistant from the poles, dividing it into the northern and southern hemispheres.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • On earth, the equator is larger than any other latitude. Hence, it is a great circle.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • As the latitudes move away from the equator towards the poles, their length decreases. The length of the earth’s equator is appx. 40090 km (approx. 24911 miles). Out of its total length, 78.7% lies across water bodies and only 21.3% lies across land. The equatorial region receives almost vertical rays of the sun throughout the year, hence the difference between the maximum and minimum range of temperature is next to zero.

The Tropic of Capricorn & Equator pass through South America.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Earth · The Tropic of Cancer: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Tropic of Cancer is 23⁰30' degrees latitude north of the equator. Due to the axial tilt of the earth and its revolution, the Tropic of Cancer (23⁰30'N latitude) starts getting oriented towards the sun by 21st March.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Three months later i.e. by 21st June the Tropic of Cancer is aligned in a way that it receives the vertical rays of the Sun. Hence 21st June is known as the day of the summer solstice in Northern Hemisphere.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Tropic of Cancer passes through the following countries/ regions of the world–

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (1) Algeria

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (2) Niger

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (3) Libya

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (4) Egypt

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (15) Mauritania

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (16) Mali

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (17) Western Sahara

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • 22nd December, when the sun is vertically overhead of The Tropic of Capricorn it is called winter solstice. Since the Earth is inclined at an angle of 23⁰30', when the sun’s rays fall at a perpendicular angle (90°) at the Tropic of Capricorn, then at the same time the Tropic of cancer will witness an inclination of90°–47°= 43°.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The angular difference between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn is 23⁰30' + 23⁰30' = 47°.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Earth · The Tropic of Capricorn: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The 23°30' South latitude in the Southern Hemisphere is known as the Tropic of Capricorn. On 21/22 December the sun shines vertically overhead the Tropic of Capricorn, and it is the longest day in the Southern Hemisphere receiving sunlight for the maximum duration.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • During this time there is low air pressure in the Southern Hemisphere and thus the region experiences summer. On in contrast the Northern Hemisphere has high air pressure and experiences winter. During this time the sun’s rays fall at an oblique angle on the Tropic of Cancer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Tropic of Capricorn passes through the following countries/regions:

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (1) Namibia

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (2) Australia

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (3) Chile

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (4) Argentina

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (11) South Africa

                                                                                                                                                                                                          (12) Madagascar.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Earth · Day & Night: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The earth has two kinds of movements – (1) Rotation i.e. rotation of Earth around its own axis. (2) Revolution i.e. the movement of the earth around the sun.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The earth on its axis rotates from west to east. The rotation of the earth causes the phenomena of Day and Night. The earth is tilted on its axis at an angle of 23.5° as a result of which the duration of Day and Night is not always equal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • However, the duration of Day and Night is always equal on the equator as the sun always shines vertically overhead on the equator.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Between 21st March and 23rd September the sun shines between the equator and the Tropic of Cancer, as a result of which the Northern Hemisphere receives more than 12 hours of sunlight. Thus the Days are longer and nights are shorter in the Northern Hemisphere during this time.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Similarly, from 23rd September to 21st March, the sun shines between the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn. As a result the Southern Hemisphere receives more than 12 hours of sunlight. As one moves closer to the South Pole the duration of Day keeps on increasing, during this period the South Pole witnesses a 6 month long daytime.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Earth revolves around the sun in an elliptical orbit and completes one revolution around the sun in approx 365 days and 6 hours. Thus because of revolution and axial tilt, the angle of insolation changes throughout the year. Solstices occur twice a year.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Summer solstice – On 20/21st June the sun shines vertically overhead at Tropic of Cancer. This phenomenon is called the summer solstice. On 20/21st June the Northern Hemisphere experiences the lengthiest day. The phenomenon is also called June solstice. During this time the Southern Hemisphere witnesses the shortest day.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Winter solstice – On 21/22nd December, the sun shines vertically overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn. This phenomenon is called the winter solstice. During this time the Southern Hemisphere witnesses the lengthiest day and Northern Hemisphere witnesses the shortest day. This phenomenon is also known as the December solstice.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • On 20/21st March The Vernal Equinox occurs and on 22/23rd September The Autumnal Equinox. During this time the length of day and night is equal. Due to the revolution and axial tilt of the Earth, the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° North Latitude) in the Northern Hemisphere starts getting oriented towards the sun from 21 March and by 21st June the sun is vertically overhead the Tropic of Cancer.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The size of the shadow of any object depends upon the size of the object, the distance from the sun and the angle it creates with respect to the rays of the sun.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The size of the shadow will be the smallest when the angle is least.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • When the angle created is 0° there will be no shadow formation.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The shadow formation in the Northern Hemisphere will be at a minimum on 21st June.
                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The group of small pieces of rock revolving round the sun between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter are called:Asteroids

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Asteroids → small rocky bodies orbiting the Sun between Mars and Jupiter (not Jupiter and Saturn); most are small, some up to 1000 km across. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the difference between asteroids and comets?1 and 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Asteroids: rocky-metallic, no tail, mostly between Mars and Jupiter. Comets: frozen gases/ice with rock, glowing tail near the Sun, from Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Comets are not found mostly between Venus and Mercury; that statement (2) is false.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The tail of comet is directed away from the Sun, because–The radiation emitted by the Sun exerts a radial pressure on the comet throwing its tail away from the Sun.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Comet's tail points away from the Sun → the Sun's radiation pressure pushes the coma's gas and dust outward.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Hale-Bopp is the name of a-Comet

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Hale-Bopp → a long-period comet discovered in 1995 by Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp, named after both.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • With which planet comet Shoemaker-Levy collide –Jupiter

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Comet Shoemaker-Levy-9 → collided with Jupiter during 16-22 July 1994 (found 24 March 1993); first collision of two solar-system bodies seen from Earth.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Meteor is a –A piece of matter which has entered the earth atmosphere from outer space

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Meteor ('shooting star') → a small piece of rock from space that glows and burns by air friction on entering Earth's atmosphere; not a star.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Correct Latitudinal position of a place that could be possible is-45° South

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Latitude is only North or South of the Equator and ends at the Poles (ninety degrees). So 'forty-five degrees South' is valid; East/West values are longitudes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which of the following is not a great circle on the globe?60° North latitude

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Great circle → divides the globe into two halves: the Equator and all meridians (Prime Meridian, any East longitude). No other parallel, e.g. sixty degrees North, is one.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Zero degree latitude and zero degree longitude lies in theAtlantic Ocean

                                                                                                                                                                                                          0° latitude meets 0° longitude (Equator × Prime Meridian) → in the Gulf of Guinea, Atlantic Ocean. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 2 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the geographical details given in the following figure:Europe

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Point near 50°30' N latitude and 5° E longitude → Belgium, so the region is Europe.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A plane starts flying from 30° northern latitude and 50° eastern longitude and lands at the opposite end of the earth, where will it land –30° Southern latitude, 130° Western longitude

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Opposite end of the Earth from 30°N, fifty degrees E → 30°S, 130°W (latitude switches N to S; longitude switches E to W).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Among the following cities which one lies in the farthest North?Rome

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Northernmost of the four → Rome (highest latitude). North to south: Rome, New York, Beijing, New Delhi.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Don't confuse Don't assume New York lies north of Rome; Rome's latitude is higher.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The country which has the longest north-south (latitudinal) extension of its territory is:None of the above/More than one of the above

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Longest north-south extent → Chile (continuous mainland) or Russia (if islands are included), so the answer was 'more than one of the above'.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • How many latitudes are there on the globe drawn at 1 degree interval?179

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Parallels drawn at 1° interval → 89 in each hemisphere + the Equator = 179.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The time at Cairo is 2 hours ahead of Greenwich. Hence, it is located at-30° E longitude

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Cairo, 2 hours ahead of Greenwich → about 30° E longitude (1° = 4 minutes; 120 minutes ÷ 4 = 30°).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid Time to longitude: minutes of time ÷ 4 = degrees of longitude.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • When it is noon along 82° 30' E longitude along what degree of longitude it will be 6.30 a.m.?At 0° East or West

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Noon at eighty-two and a half degrees E (IST meridian) = 6:30 a.m. at 0° (Prime Meridian): the 5 hours 30 minutes gap equals that whole longitude.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If the difference of longitudes for the two places is 90°, the time interval between these places will be –6 hr

                                                                                                                                                                                                          90° difference in longitude → 6 hours time difference (90 × 4 = 360 minutes).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • When, there is mid-day in the Greenwich, local time of a place is 5 O'clock evening. At which of the following longitude (meridians) that place will be located –75° E

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Mid-day at Greenwich and 5 p.m. at a place → 5 hours (300 minutes) ahead, so it lies east: 300 ÷ 4 = seventy-five degrees East.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following longitudes along with the Prime Meridian forms a great circle on the globe.180°

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Prime Meridian (0°, Greenwich; accepted 1884) + the 180° meridian (International Date Line) together form one great circle.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In the New Millennium, the first ray of the Sun was seen in which of the following Meridians of India –93° 30'E

                                                                                                                                                                                                          First sunrise of the New Millennium in India → Katchal Island (Andaman and Nicobar), about 1600 km from the mainland and 418 km from Port Blair.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The basis of deciding the standard time of any place is–Prime Meridian

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Standard time base → Prime Meridian (0°, Greenwich). It crosses UK, France, Spain, Algeria, Mali, Burkina-Faso, Togo, Ghana; not Niger, Nigeria or Portugal. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 3 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Time of which of the following places is equal to the time of GMT.1, 2 and 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                          GMT time is used in Accra (Ghana), Dublin (Ireland) and Lisbon (Portugal); not in Madrid (Spain).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following cities does not have the same clock time as that of the other three Cities at any given instant?Addis Ababa (Ethiopia)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          London, Lisbon and Accra share GMT; Addis Ababa (Ethiopia) is the odd one: its standard time is 3 hours ahead of GMT.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The standard time of the following countries is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time depending on whether they are East or West of the longitude passing through Greenwich.5, 3, 2, 1, 4

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Ahead to behind GMT: Japan +9, Iraq +3, Greece +2, Cuba –5, Costa Rica –6 hours (order 5, 3, 2, 1, 4).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • When there is noon at I.S.T. meridian people another place of the Earth is taking their 6 O'clock morning tea. The longitude of the place is:7°30' W

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Noon on the IST meridian, 6 a.m. tea elsewhere → 6 hours = 90° west of IST → the place is at 7°30' W.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A telegram was sent from Greenwich at 12.00 Noon. The time for transmission was 12 minutes. It reached a town at 6.00 p.m. The longitude of the town will be:87° E

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Telegram sent at noon from Greenwich, 12 minutes in transit, arrives 6 p.m. → 348 minutes of time gap ÷ 4 = 87° E.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • International Date Line passes through –Pacific ocean

                                                                                                                                                                                                          International Date Line → runs through the Pacific Ocean, opposite Greenwich; separates two calendar days and bends where land falls in its way.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Statement (A): Time interval at the date-line is 12 hours from the Greenwich.(A), (R) both are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Date Line lies on the meridian opposite Greenwich → 12 hours (720 minutes) time gap from Greenwich: A and R both true, R explains A.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • There is no minimum distance between two places on the globe:International Date Line

                                                                                                                                                                                                          No 'minimum distance' between two places → along the International Date Line, because it is bent (turned at 8 places, e.g. near Alaska).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • If the earth's direction of rotation is reversed, what should be the IST when it is noon at the International Date Line?06.30 hrs

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Rotation reversed → IST = GMT – 5:30. Noon at the Date Line = midnight GMT, so IST = 6:30 p.m. (18.30 hrs).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following Straits is nearest to the International Date Line?Bering Strait

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Strait nearest the International Date Line → Bering Strait; Malacca, Florida and Gibraltar straits lie far from it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • A ship is moving from the eastern side of Aleutian Islands towards Dutch Harbour. It crosses 180° meridian on 1st January 1999 at 23:30 hr. What time and date will be recorded by the captain of the ship in his diary after one-hour journey from the point of crossing of the meridian?January 2, 00:30 hr

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Ship crossing the 180 meridian (Aleutians to Dutch Harbour) at 23:30, 1 January 1999 → logs 00:30, 2 January: the Date Line bends around them, so no date change.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Captain of a ship moving Westward records the local time of 10-00 hrs Monday at 90° W. If the speed of the ship is the same as the speed of the rotation of the earth, which of the following local time and day would be found by the captain at International date line:10.00 Monday

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Ship sailing west at Earth's rotation speed, 10:00 Monday at 90° W → still 10:00 Monday on reaching the Date Line; 10:00 Tuesday after crossing it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Consider the following statements:I only

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Anadyr (Siberia) and Nome (Alaska), about 800 km apart across the Date Line → breakfasts fall on different days; Nome is same day or behind, never ahead. Only I correct.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which path must be followed by a Ship to move from one place to another in the least time?Meridian

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Least-time route for a ship between two places → along the Meridian (book's answer; not sea currents or sea-breeze).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The local time of a place is 6:00 AM when the Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is 3:00 AM, what is the longitude of the place?45° East

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Local time 6:00 AM when GMT is 3:00 AM → 3 hours ahead → 15 × 3 = 45° East. Must know

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Memory aid 1 hour = 15° of longitude; 1° = 4 minutes; east is ahead, west is behind.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • What is the local time of Thimphu (Bhutan) located at 90° East longitude when the time at Greenwich (0°) is 12:00 noon:6:00 p.m.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Thimphu (Bhutan, 90° E) when Greenwich is 12 noon → 90 × 4 = 360 minutes = 6 hours ahead → 6:00 p.m.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following is not a natural unit of time?Standard time

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Standard time is man-made (e.g. India uses the 82½° E line), not a natural unit; tropical year, lunar month and day are natural units of time.

So four countries.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The total length of Earth’s equator is about –40,000 km

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Equator length → about 40,000 km (40090 km); 78.7% of it passes over water, 21.3% over land.

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Through which, one of the following groups of countries does the Equator pass?Colombia, Kenya and Indonesia

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The latitude at which ‘Annual Range of Temperature remains minimum is –Equator

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Which one of the following cities is nearest to the equator?Singapore

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Equator, Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn, all the three pass through which one of the following Continents?Africa

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), a low pressure zone, is located.at the equator

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • At the Winter Solstice the noon altitude of the Sun at the Tropic of Cancer is:43.0°

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Winter solstice (about 22 December): Sun overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn; noon Sun's altitude at the Tropic of Cancer = 43.0° (the tropics are 47° apart).

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Tropic of Cancer does not pass through Iran.                                                                                                                                                                                                           • Which of the following statements is true regarding earth movement?Both 1 and 2 are false

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Tropic of Capricorn does not pass through –Bolivia

                                                                                                                                                                                                          Tropic of Capricorn crosses Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina, Chile, Namibia, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique, Madagascar, Australia (also French Polynesia, Tonga); not Bolivia.                                                                                                                                                                                                           • Which of the following phenomenon happens in India when the sun-shines vertically over the Tropic of Capricorn?High pressure develops over North-West India

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • On which date day and night are of equal duration?23 September

                                                                                                                                                                                                          • At the time the summer solstice in the northern hemisphere the length of the day will be 12 hours at the:Equator
