                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Rivers of the World: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River is known as ‘cradle of civilization’ and Asia is known as birthplace of every religion.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Mesopotamian civilization nurtured in the region enclosed by the Dajla-Farat (Tigris-Euphrates) river system and the Harappa civilization prospered in Indus River System.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The longest river in Asia is the Yangtze River which flows through China and drains into the Pacific Ocean. The Yangtze is 6300 km long.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Mekong River has its source in the Tibetan Plateau from where it runs through China’s Yunnan Province, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam and finally drains into the South China Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The river Salween has its source in the Tibetan plateau from where it flows into Myanmar, and drains into the Gulf of Martaban of Andaman Sea is south-east Asia after travelling a distance of 2815 km.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • It Makes border between Myanmar and Thailand.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The river Amur is 2897 km (4440 km. if the argun river is included) long. It creates the border between Mangolia, Russia and China before it drains into the Pacific ocean (near Tatar strait).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Indus is the most important river of Pakistan. River Indus is joined by rivers - Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej, Kabul etc. before it drains into the Arabian Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Irrawaddy is called the lifeline of the country Myanmar. River Huang Ho is a river that flows through the Northern part of China. The basin of this river is the birthplace of the ancient Chinese civilization. The river is also called the yellow river, because of the yellow coloured soil found in this region.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Mahaweli Ganga (335 km) is the longest river in Sri Lanka. It flows in North-East direction and drains into the Bay of Bengal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The River Tigris rises in the Taurus Mountains of Eastern Turkiye. The river flows south Turkiye and then through Syria (Syria - Turkiye border). Tigris is joined by River Euphrates in Iraq and then the collective stream drains into the Persian Gulf near Basra.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Amu Darya and Syr Darya are two important rivers of Central Asia. Both the rivers have different sources from where they emerge but both drain into the Aral Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Amur, Ob and Lena are important rivers of Russia which Amur flows in North-east direction and Ob and Lena flow in northward from their source.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Volga is the longest river in Europe. It rises in the Valdai hills and drains in the Caspian Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Danube is the second longest river after Volga. It originates in Germany and drains into the Black Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Dnieper originates in the western parts of Moscow and drains into the Black sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Ural originates in the southern Ural mountains and discharges into the Caspian Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Rhine originates from the Swiss Alps. The river flows through a rift valley and drains into the North Sea. The famous city of Bonn (Germany) is situated on the bank of the River Rhine.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Rhine is the busiest inland waterway of Europe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Po is the most important river of Italy, also known as the Ganga of Italy. It is also the longest river in Italy.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Tiber rises in the Apennine Mountains (Italy) and drains into the Tyrrhenian sea. The city of Rome is situated on the bank of this river.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Don rises from the western Russian near the city of Tula oblast and drains into the Sea of Azov.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Ebro of Spain originates in the Cantabrian Mountains and drains into the Mediterranean Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Thames is the longest river of England and the second longest in the United Kingdom after the River Severn.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Nile is a major river in North-Eastern Africa (app. 6695 km). It is an international river. 10 countries of Nile basin Initiative namely- Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Sudan and Egypt are the member of the Nile Basin initiative (NBI) and Eritrea is an observer. The River finally drains into the Mediterranean sea. The River originates from the Victoria Lake as White Nile. Here it is known as Victoria Nile. However, the latest’s researches conducted have stated that the actual source of white Nile is in Nyungwe Forests located near lake Kivu in south-western Rawanda. The Blue Nile is the most important tributary of white Nile. The Blue Nile originates at Lake Tana in Ethiopia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The White Nile and the Blue Nile meet in the Sudan capital of Khartoum and the collective water body is known as the River Nile. The fertile silt and abundance of fresh water from the river is most cherished by the country Egypt. As a result, Egypt is also known as the Gift of Nile. The River Nile is like an Oasis for those arid regions that fall in her course.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Niger is a river in West Africa that rises from Fouta Djallon Highlands and discharges into the Gulf of Guinea Major Rivers of the World in the Atlantic Ocean.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Limpopo of Africa crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Congo River known as the River Zaire is the second longest river in Africa and has a total length of about 4374 km. It crosses the equator twice. Victoria Falls is a waterfall on the River Zambezi. The Kariba Dam has been constructed on this river.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The essential rivers of North America are- St. Lawrence, Yukon, Missouri, Mississippi, Colorado, Mackenzie, Columbia, Hudson, Nelson and Fraser.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The source of river Mississippi is the Lake Itasca in Minnesota. Ohio, Arkansas and Red river are the main tributaries of the river Mississippi. The Mississippi River drains into the Gulf of Mexico. It is noteworthy to mention that the Great Plains of North America were formed by the Mississippi and Missouri rivers. The Mississippi - Missouri Jefferson river system is the largest river system in North America. Its total length is 6275 km.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Yukon is a river in North America that flows through the state of Alaska (U.S.A.) and Canada. The upper half of the river flows through Canada. Its total length is 3185 km.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Mackenzie River is the longest river in Canada. The river originates in the Great Slave Lake of North-western Canada and drains into the Arctic Ocean. The total length of the river Mackenzie is 1738 km.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Saint Lawrence River connects the Great Lakes to Atlantic Ocean. The river is part of the international boundary between the United States of America and Canada.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Rio Grande is a part of the International border between USA and Mexico. It drains into the Gulf of Mexico.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Columbia originates in the Rocky Mountains of British Columbia (Canada) and drains into the Pacific Ocean.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Hudson originates in the Adirondack Mountains of New York (USA) and drains into the Atlantic Ocean.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Orinoco, Amazon and La Plata Basin form the major portion of the Plains of South America. The Amazon River of South America is the longest river on the continent and is the largest river in the world both in terms of volume and drainage area covered. Its length is 6437 km and is navigable up to 1600 km. The Orinoco River Basin is Venezuela (65%) and the remaining portion is in Colombia (35%). Parana River originates in the Brazilian Highlands.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Murray and Darling River are the two most important rivers in Australia. The Murray-Darling Valley is the most important agrarian region in Australia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The three longest rivers in the world are as follows:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          (1) Nile River (6695 km), (2) Amazon River (6437 km), (3) Yangtze River (6300 km).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Seine flows through northern France and is the second longest river in France after the Loire.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           • River Manzanares is an important river in Spain that flows through its capital Madrid.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Potomac flows from Maryland to Washington D.C. and finally drains into the Chesapeake Bay.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • River Huangpu is 113 km long and flows through Shanghai.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Phnom Penh is the capital of Cambodia. The city is situated on the banks of the river Mekong.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam. The city mostly lies on the right bank of the Red River.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Yangon is the former capital of Myanmar.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           • The Danube is an important river in Europe.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           Landforms by River: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In rivers, erosion, transportation and deposition go on simultaneously from the point of origin to the point where they meet the sea. This process leads to the formation of different terrestrial relief features. Some of them are as follows Gorge - It is a deep narrow section of river valley usually with near vertical rock walls, more generally a narrow valley between hills and mountains. Gorges are formed as a result of continued erosion of mountainous terrain by a river. For Ex: Chisapani Gorge in Nepal is formed by Karnali River. Karnali is the longest river in Nepal (507 km). It is due to the high velocity of the river that it creates many gorges. Canyon- Canyons are the more eroded version of gorges. Grand Canyon is located in Arizona (US). It is a steep-sided canyon carved by Colorado River. The canyon is 446/447 km long with an average width of 6.4 to 29 km and depth of 1.8 km deep.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          V-shaped Valley- V-shaped valleys are formed by erosion. The majority of the rivers in the world carry on two processes simultaneously i.e. vertical and horizontal erosion respectively. These rivers create V-shaped valleys.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Waterfalls- A waterfall is a stream that falls from a height. Waterfalls are often the sites of the greatest concentration of energy dissipation along the course of a stream.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Meanders- As water flowing under gravity seldom flows straight for any long distance, a winding course soon appears. The irregularities of the ground force the river to swing in loops, forming meanders.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Alluvial Cones - Also called alluvial fans, they are cone shaped deposits of sediments built by a stream where it merges into a broad valley or plain.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Delta- When the river reaches the sea, the fine materials it has not yet dropped are deposited at its mouth, forming a fan-shaped alluvial area called a delta. This alluvial tract is, in fact, a seaward extension of the floodplains. Deltas differ much in size, shape, growth and importance. A number of factors such as the rate of sedimentation the depth of the river, the sea bed and the character of tides, currents and waves greatly influence the eventual formation of deltas. The Ganges Delta is the largest delta in the world. It is also known as Ganges-Brahmaputra, Meghna Delta or Sunderban Delta.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Formation of delta is affected by:Deep sea

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Islands: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • An island is a piece of land surrounded on all sides by water. It may occur individually or in a group, in open oceans or seas. Smaller ones of only local significance are found even in lakes and rivers. Islands can be grouped under the following types- (a) Continental Islands (b) Oceanic Islands.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Greenland is the world’s largest (2166086 sq. km.) island. Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Nuuk is the capital and the largest city of Greenland. Nuuk has an elevation of1-3 m above sea level.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • New Guinea is the second largest (785753 sq. km.) island in the world, located north of Australia. It is separated from the Australian mainland by Torres Strait.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Borneo is the third largest island in the world and the largest in Asia, located north of Java Sea. The island is politically divided among three countries- Indonesia (73%), Malaysia (26%) and Brunei (1%). The Kalimantan region of Indonesia is a part of Borneo islands.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Madagascar is an island country located in the Southwestern Indian Ocean, off the coast of East Africa. To the east of Madagascar, we have the island country of Mauritius and to the west, we have the African country of Mozambique. Madagascar is the fourth largest (587041 sq. km.) island in the world.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Diego Garcia is an island in the Indian Ocean. The island is named after the Portuguese explorer Diego Garcia who discovered it in the early 16th century. From 1814 to 1965 the island was a part of colonial Mauritius, later it became a dependency of the British Colony. In 1966, the United Kingdom leased it to the United States. At present, Diego Garcia is an active military base far the both US and UK.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Seychelles is an island situated to the north of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean. The island group comprises 115 islands, some of which are made up of corals and granite.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Chagos Islands are located in the Indian Ocean. Diego Garcia is the largest island of Chagos Archipelago.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Mauritius is an island nation, located to the east of Madagascar in the Indian Ocean.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Socotra Island is located in the Indian Ocean between 12°30’ North latitude and 54° East Longitude. The island is officially a part of Yemen.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The island of Indonesia extends from Aceh in the west to Torres Strait (a Strait that lies between Australia and the Melanesian island of New Guinea) in the east. Indonesia is an island country in Southeast Asia between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. There are 17508 islands in Indonesia. Out of the 17508 islands only 1000 have been inhabited.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Fiji is an island country in the Pacific Ocean. Fiji lies to the east of Vanuatu, west of Tonga and the south of Tuvalu.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Fiji comprises 333 islands but approx. 87% of its population is concentrated on two islands Viti Levu and Vanua Levu.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Falkland Archipelago is an Island group in South Atlantic Ocean, located at a distance of 650 km from the mainland of South America.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Azores Island are an autonomous region of Portugal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Cape Verde Island and the Bahamas are located in the Atlantic Ocean.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Macau is located approx. 64 km to the west of Hong Kong and is attached to mainland China.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Grenada is an island country in the southeastern caribbean Sea. Grenada consists of three islands - Grenada, carriacou and Petite Martinique which form the southern end of the Windward Islands. The island is also known as ‘Island of Spices’ because of the heavy production of the same. The island is located on the North Coast of Venezuela at a distance of 160 km.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Balearic Islands are an archipelago of Spain in the western Mediterranean Sea. It is an autonomous community and a province of Spain. The flag of the Balearic Islands is distinct from that of Spain. The Balearic archipelago consists of 4 major islands. The capital of this island is Palma de Mallorca. Balearic island was a part of Spain since 1833 A.D. but in 1983 they became an autonomous region.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Melanesia is a sub-region of Oceania extending from Papua New Guinea in the South western Pacific Ocean to the Arafura Sea and then eastward to Fiji. The important islands of the region are- New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, Santa Cruz Islands, Vanuatu, Solomon, Fiji and New Caledonia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Australian continent is an island continent. It is the smallest continent and is completely under thejurisdiction of the sovereign state of Australia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Japan is located in the Pacific Ocean to the east of the Asian mainland. It is a country of about 14125 islands (at least 100m circumference) of these only four are large and important. In order of their size, they are Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and Shikoku. Hokkaido is the northernmost island of Japan among these four islands and occupies an approx. area of83453.57 km². In the middle is Honshu occupying an area of 228000 km² and in the southwestern part the islands of Kyushu and Shikoku are located.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The capital of Japan
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • i.e. Tokyo is located on Honshu Island.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Majuli island is the largest river Island in the world, located in the Brahmaputra River, in the state of Assam (India).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Faroe Islands are also known as sheep islands. They are located to the south of Norwegian Sea in North Atlantic Ocean. It is an autonomous country of the Kingdom of Denmark. The Faroe Archipelago consists of 18 mountainous islands.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Lakes and Water Falls: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Lakes are among the most varied features of the earth’s surface. They occupy the hollow of the land surface in which water accumulates.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Important lakes of the world include
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • – Caspian Sea, Lake Chad, lakes of U.S.A. and Canada (Lake Superior, Michigan Huron, Erie and Ontario), Lake Victoria, Aral Sea, Lake Nyasa, Lake Baikal, Great Bear Lake, Lake Titicaca, Dead Sea, Lake Crater, etc. Based on the total area occupied and volume, the largest lake in the world is the Caspian Sea of Eurasia. The lake covers an area of 371000 km². Caspian is a brackish water lake. The Ural and Volga rivers drain into its northern part. To the south of the Caspian Sea is the Kara-Bogaz Bay which has a salinity of approx 300-350‰. The Great Lakes of North America are located in the east-central part of the continent.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Lake Superior is the world’s largest freshwater Lake (Note - Lake Huron and Michigan are technically a single lake. On this basis lake Huron-Michigan is the largest freshwater lake by surface area in the world). It is one of the great lakes located between USA and Canada.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Lake Baikal of Russia is the World’s deepest lake having a maximum depth of 1642 meter. Baikal is about 25 million years old. Lake Baikal is also known as the Sacred Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Lake Tanganyika is the world’s second deepest lake at 1470 meters. It is also the world’s longest freshwater lake (670 km).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Lake Titicaca is located on the border of Peru and Bolivia. It is the highest navigable lake in the world. It is 280 meters (919 feet) deep.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Lake Victoria is located between Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Dead Sea is a salt lake bordered by Jordan, Israel and Palestine (West Bank occupied by Israel).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Aral Sea is a salt water lake on the borders of Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. Lake Van is the most saline lake in the world, with salinity reaching as high as 330‰ (according to Savindra Singh Book). Lake Van is located in Turkiye. Great Slave, Great Bear, Reindeer, Winnipeg, and Athabasca are some of the important lakes in Canada.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Uranium City is located near Lake Athabasca.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Boiling Lake is located in Dominica.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Red Lagoon is in Bolivia close to the Chilean border and Lake Urmia is in Iran.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Finger Lakes are a group of small lakes located in New York State.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Five Flower Lake is located in Sichuan Province China.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Finland is a Nordic country located in Northern Europe. Finland is known as the 'Garden of Lakes'/'Land of Thousand Lakes'.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Lake Saimaa is the largest lake in Finland and fourth largest natural freshwater lake in Europe. Cities that are located near the Great Lakes of North America are – Duluth near Lake Superior (North America), Chicago near Lake Michigan, and Buffalo near Lake Erie. The city of Detroit is located on the banks of Detroit River.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Lakes are water bodies surrounded by land on all sides. They vary tremendously in size, shape, depth and mode of formation. Hence keeping in mind the various competitive examinations, the following relevant facts have been provided regarding lakes-

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                WORLD

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 The largest freshwater lake –

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                By volume-Lake Baikal,

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                by the total surface area covered - Lake Superior.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Largest saltwater lake – Caspian Sea (Russia, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Kazakhstan)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Largest lake in the world – Caspian Sea.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Most saline lake in the world – Lake Assal (Djibouti).  Lake with the lowest elevation – Dead Sea (Jordan, Israel & West Bank)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Highest lake in the world – Ojos del Salado (Chile - Argentina)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 The highest navigable lake in the world – Lake Titicaca (Peru, Bolivia).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                LAGOON

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A lagoon is a body of water separated from larger bodies of water by a natural barrier. Natural barriers may include sandbars, barrier reefs, coral reefs, etc. Chilika (Odisha) is the largest lagoon in India whereas the New Caledonian barrier reef (in New Caledonia an overseas region of France) is the largest lagoon in the world.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Great Lakes of North America and the important cities located near them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The great lakes of North America consist of five lakes – Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Superior, Lake Ontario and Lake Erie. These lakes are known for their industrial clusters and inland navigation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Lake Superior, Lake Huron, Erie and Ontario create the border between USA and Canada.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • When rivers plunge down in a sudden fall of some height, they are called waterfalls.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The highest waterfall in the world is Salto Angel (979 m). The waterfall is located on Rio Churun which is a tributary of the river Rio Carrao which flows through Canaima National Park in Venezuela. 'Rio Carrao is a tributary of Rio Orinoco.'
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Tugela waterfalls is located on the river Tugela in South Africa.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Victoria Falls lies in South-Central Africa on the borders of Zambia and Zimbabwe. The falls are located on the river Zambezi. In 1989 it was included in the list of World Heritage Sites.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Ribbon falls is located on the river Ribbon Creek in Yosemite National Park in California. It is 491m high.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Niagara Falls is located on the river Niagara on the international border between Canada and USA.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Browne Falls (836 m) is located in New Zealand.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Straits: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • A strait is a narrow passage of water connecting two seas or two other large water bodies and simultaneously separating two landmasses.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Bering Strait separates Asia from North America. The strait is 85 km wide and joins the Chukchi Sea (part of the Arctic Ocean) in the north to Bering Sea in the south.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Gibraltar separates Europe from Africa andjoins the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Dover Strait joins the English Channel to the North Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Dover Strait is located in the eastern part of the English Channel. Three underwater tunnels for railways have been built here to join England to France.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Palk Strait separates Tamil Nadu from Sri Lanka. It joins the Bay of Bengal (Palk Bay) to Gulf of Mannar. The strait is 64-137 km wide. Palk Strait has been named after Robert Palk who was the governor of Madras Presidency from 1763 to 1767.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Hormuz Strait is a strait between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       The Canals: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A canal is a manmade waterway that allows boats and ships to pass from one body of water to another. Canals are also used to transport water for irrigation and other human uses.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Suez Canal has been constructed on the Isthmus of Suez and is the longest man-made canal in the world. It was 164 km long in 1869 and 193.30 km. in 2015.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Suez Canal was opened for navigation in the year 1869. It connects the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea. The canal was very instrumental in reducing the travel distance between Europe and Asia. It reduced the distance between Europe and India by 7000 km. Suez is the largest navigable canal in the world.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Panama Canal of Central America joins the Pacific Ocean to the Atlantic Ocean. Prior to the construction of this canal one had to circle around both the Americas i.e. North America and South America, to reach the city of New York located on the eastern coast of USA, from San Francisco located on the West Coast of USA. Panama Canal is under the authority of the country of Panama.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Kiel Canal connects the North Sea to Baltic Sea. Located in Germany it is one of the busiest canal in the world.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Soo Canal connects two of the five Great Lakes of North America. These two lakes are Lake Superior and Lake Huron.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Erie canal connect Lake Erie to Hudson River.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Welland Canal connects Lake Erie to Lake Ontario.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Stalin canal (White Sea – Baltic Canal) connects the Baltic Sea to Arctic Sea.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Rhine-Main-Danube canal connects the North Sea to the Black Sea. St. Lawrence Canal is connected to the Great Lakes of North America to Atlantic Ocean and provides inland navigation to Marine ships.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A lock is a mechanism used in a river, canal, or lake for lowering or raising different boats, ships etc. Locks are constructed on those water bodies that have a high level of fluctuation in their water levels. Using the lock mechanism a river or a canal can easily be made navigable.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Locks are used in the Panama Canal, River Danube and River Rhine whereas there are no locks in the Suez Canal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The Important Dams of the World: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A dam is a barrier used to hold back running water, thus creating a reservoir that can be used for irrigation, hydroelectricity generation, drinking water, etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Parana River flows close to the borders of Brazil - Paraguay and Paraguay-Argentina Itaipu Dam has been constructed on this river which is a joint project of Brazil and Paraguay. It is 196 m high and 7919 m long.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Aswan Dam is located in Egypt on the Nile River.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Hoover dam, which was earlier known as Boulder Dam, is a dam in the Black Canyon of the Colorado river, on the border between Arizona and Nevada.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Kariba Dam is a dam on the Zambezi River, is located on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Nurek Dam is a dam on the Vakhsh river in Tajikistan.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The dam is located at a distance of 75 km from Dushanbe, the capital of Tajikistan. It is 300 m high.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The Coral Reefs: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Coral reefs are called the rainforest of the ocean.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Coral reefs are found in abundance in the tropical latitudes i.e. between Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn (generally extending between 30°N to 30°S). They occur in shallow tropical areas where the seawater is clean, clear and warm.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Coral reefs, constitute only about 0.2% of the seafloor, however, they provide for 25% of the oceanic flora and fauna.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Coral is actually a living organism.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • When the temperature rises the corals start removing the zooxanthellae from their bodies. As a result, the corals turn white and this phenomenon is called coral bleaching.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef in the world. It is located in the Pacific Ocean, North-East of the Australian state of Queensland. The Great Barrier Reef supports extraordinary biodiversity, including more than 450 species of hard coral, 1625 species of fish and over 3000 species of molluscs.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Fringing reefs are comparatively narrower. This reefsystem lies close to the shore hence, wherever the river meets the ocean the fringing reef breaks. Fringing reefs are found in South Florida, Malaysia, etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • An atoll is a ring shaped coral reef that sometimes looks like a horseshoe. Atolls are found in Antilles sea, Red sea, Indonesia Sea, China Sea and Australian Sea. Funafuti Atoll is a famous atoll.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The Atmosphere: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • ∗The atmosphere is made up of different gases. Among all these gases oxygen and carbon dioxide are important for the existence of humans and plants respectively.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The atmosphere is composed of various gases, of which 99% is made up of nitrogen and oxygen. Other 1% comprises argon, carbon dioxide, neon, krypton, helium, Hydrogen, and xenon.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Gas Formula Presence in Atmosphere (in percentage)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      NitrogenN₂78.084
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      OxygenO₂20.947
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ArgonAr0.934
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Carbon dioxideCO₂0.0426
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      NeonNe0.0018
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      HeliumHe0.0005
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      KryptonKr0.0001
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      HydrogenH₂0.000053
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      XenonXe0.000009

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ∗Heavy gases in the atmosphere descend whereas lighter gases are found in the upper layers as they ascend. As a result CO₂ gases extend up to 20 km from the surface, oxygen, and nitrogen up to 100 km, hydrogen up to 125 km and other gases rise far above 125 km except ozone. The atmosphere is made up of different layers of gases with varying densities and temperatures. Based on these factors different layers of the atmosphere are as follows-

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (1) Troposphere – The lowest layer of the atmosphere is called troposphere. All weather activities like clouds, hail, fog, blizzards, thunder, windstorms, etc. are confined to the troposphere. The most important characteristic of the troposphere is that there is a decrease of 6.5° C with an increase of every 1000 min altitude. This decrease in temperature with an increase in altitude is known as normal lapse rate. The upper boundary of the troposphere is called tropopause.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (2) Stratosphere – Stratosphere (15-50 km) is the second most important layer of the atmosphere. It lies between mesosphere (above) and troposphere (below). This layer of atmosphere is very dry in nature and has the least amount of water vapor in it. As a result, there is no weather activity in stratosphere. The stratosphere is used for aviation purposes as the absence of weather activities makes this layer ideal for flying. Ozone layer is found in this sphere.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (3) Mesosphere – This layer is found at an altitude of 50 to 80 km. The upper ceiling of mesosphere is called mesopause.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • (4) Ionosphere – It is an electrically conducting layer, that makes radio wave transmission possible over long distances. Ionosphere extends from 80 to 640 km.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The unique feature of Ionosphere is the phenomenon of Aurora Borealis in Northern Hemisphere and Aurora Australis in Southern Hemisphere.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (5) Exosphere – It is the topmost layer of the atmosphere and is situated above the ionosphere. This layer has no defined boundary. The Communication satellites are positioned in the exosphere.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The Insolation to The Local Winds
