                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The Major Tribes of the World: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Tribal peoples are those groups of people who are similar to each other on the basis of social customs, language and culture.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Nomadic Tribes are those groups of people that travel from one place to another to find fodder for their cattle. Though nomadic tribes are found all over the world, they are mostly concentrated in arid regions. They are primarily found in the arid regions of Africa, Central Asia, and South America.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • When people shift from one location to another in a particular season and then return to the same location after that season is over, it is called seasonal migration For example when it starts to snow in the mountains the tribal people shift to the valley and return after the winter season is over.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Gaddi, Bakarwal and Bhotia are some of the tribes of India that practice seasonal migration.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Pygmy Tribe is found in the rainforests of Congo Basin in Equatorial Africa. They are hunters and gatherers. They construct huts at the tops of trees which are called Mongulu. They are black short- statured people of Negrito race.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Eskimo tribes are found in the tundra regions of Alaska, Canada and Greenland. They are of Mongoloid race and hunting is their main occupation. They use a weapon called the harpoon and a Yayak boat to catch fish.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Inuit is a cultural group of indigenous people found in Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland (Denmark), Russia and Alaska.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Maasai tribes are found in the plateau regions of East Africa which include Kenya, northern Tanzania and eastern Uganda. They are cattle herders and their main occupation is cattle rearing. They live in huts called Kraal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Bushman Tribe is found in desert regions of Kalahari which include South Africa, Zimbabwe, Eswatini, Botswana, Namibia, etc Hunting and gathering is their main occupation. They are omnivorous. Termites are called the rice of Bushman.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Zulu tribes reside in South Africa. They are known for their culture and rituals. The Battle of Isandlwana was fought between the British and Zulu tribe in 1879. The tribe practices agriculture and cattle rearing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Semang tribe resides on the island of Malay in Malaysia. They belong to Negrito race and depend on hunting and gathering.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Sakai tribe is found in the forests of the Malay Peninsula, Malaysia and Indonesia. They use blowpipes for hunting.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Papua tribes reside in Papua New Guinea (Pacific Ocean). They practice agriculture and cattle rearing.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Sami tribe (Lapps tribe) is found in Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Kola Peninsula in Russia. The region is also known as Fenno Scandinavia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Bedouin tribes are found in the desert regions of Arabia, especially in the northern part of Saudi Arabia. Living in tribal groups they practice a migratory lifestyle. They belong to Armenoids and Mediterranean (Caucasian) races.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • The Bora tribe is found in the coastal areas of Western Amazon Basin, Brazil, Peru and Colombia. They practice primitive agriculture and are known to be cruel in nature.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Kirghiz tribe is a group in Central Asia spread between Pamir Plateau in Kyrgyzstan and the Tianshan mountain range. Kirghiz tribes are cattle rearing tribes that practice seasonal migration. They build round shaped temporary tents known as Yurts.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Yupik tribe is found in Eastern Russia and Western Alaska. The tribe uses sledges (ice carts driven by dogs).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Yukaghir is a Mongoloid tribe found in Verkhoyansk (North-East Siberia) and Stanovoy Mountains.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Maya tribe is found in Central America, mainly in Mexico, Guatemala and Honduras.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Maori is a Polynesian tribe residing in New Zealand. Their main occupation is agriculture and gathering.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Among the other tribes of the world – Fulani tribes reside in West Africa, Bantu tribe resides in eastern, southern and central Africa, Nuba tribe resides in Sudan, Vedda tribe is found in Sri Lanka, Barber tribe resides in Morocco and north Africa Enu tribe resides in Japan and Aeta tribe is found in the Philippines.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Important tribes of India are – Oran, Gond, Kol, Santhal, Bheel and Toda.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • India is believed to be the indigenous place of the Gypsy. The Gypsy people are believed to be associated with dome Caste (Scheduled Caste) of India.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Archaeopteryx was the first bird to emerge on Earth somewhere around 150 million years ago.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Africa is believed to be the birthplace of Mankind. At present, Caucasian race is counted amongthe largest races on Earth. They have straight or curly hairs, dark blue or brown eyes and a cranial Index of80 and above. Hobble and Elliot Smith have categorized Caucasians in to three groups
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • – Nordic, Alpine and Mediterranean.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Caucasians are the largest group in the world.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Mongoloid race is mostly found in Central and Eastern Asia. They have yellowish and brown skin and a small forehead.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Negroids are dark brown to brown in appearance. Africa is their indigenous place.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Cro-Magnon is believed to be the most modern of the human species. It existed up to the emergence of the present modern man i.e. Homo sapiens. The first evidence of Cro-Magnon was found in an excavation in France in Dordogne Valley in 1868. It is believed that Cro Magnon dates from the Upper Paleolithic Period (40000 to 10000 years ago).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Economic Geography: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              A. Agriculture & Livestock

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Grains are the main source of food for humankind. The important grains are Rice, Wheat, Corn, Millet, Barley, Chickpea, and Pulses etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Rice is cultivated in tropical, semitropical and temperate regions. Hence rice is grown in most of the wet humid areas of the world, although it can be grown in arid regions also with the help of irrigation. In most areas around the world, rice is grown as a Kharif crop, which is harvested in Nov.-Dec., but in Java, it is harvested in April-May. The International Rice Gene Bank, maintained by International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) is located in Los Banos (Philippines). IRRI was established in the year 1960. Paddy is very famous in China. Out of the total area under rice cultivation in China halfis used to cultivate hybrid rice.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to FAO, 2024 India has the maximum area under rice cultivation (50.51 million hectare) followed by China (29.26 million hectare). Despite having less area under rice cultivation, China has a total area under irrigation whereas in India only half of the area under rice cultivation is irrigated. According to Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) 2024 the four leading producers of rice in the world are - 1. India (217.87 million tonnes), 2. China (207.53 million tonnes), 3. Bangladesh (60.57 million tonnes), 4. Indonesia (53.14 million tonnes) and 5. Vietnam (43.45 million tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to latest updates – from FAO 2024, Tajikistan has the largest productivity of rice (13385.8 kg/ha) followed by Australia (11914.4 kg/ha).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Wheat is basically a temperate crop. Its cultivation spreads up to 60° latitudes in Northern Hemisphere and up to 40° latitudes in Southern Hemisphere. Wheat requires an average temperature of 10°C during germination and an average temperature between 15°-20°C during the development of grains. A Timely rainfall between 20 cm and 70 cm is also required.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to FAO, 2024 the top four leading producers of wheat in the world are – China (140.10 million tonnes), India (113.29 million tonnes), Russia (82.59 million tonnes) and the USA (53.65 million tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Sugarcane requires a tropical as well as subtropical climate where the average temperature is between 21°C-27°C with average rainfall between 75 cm 150 cm. Pakistan (84.24 million tonnes), 5. Thailand (82.44 million tonnes).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Cotton is a tropical and subtropical plant.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               • According to FAO 2024, the top 5 leading producers of bananas in the world are – India (37.61 million tonnes), China (11.76 million tonnes), Indonesia (9.26 million tonnes), Ecuador (7.56 million tonnes) and Brazil (7.05 million tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to FAO 2024, the top 4 leading producers of coconut (shell) in the world are – 1. Indonesia (17.99 million tonnes), 2. India (14.71 million tonnes), 3. Philippines (14.50 million tonnes) and 4. Brazil (3.16 million tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Tobacco cultivation requires high temperatures. It grows well between 21° to 27°C. Tobacco requires an annual average rainfall of100 to 120 centimeters. According to FAO 2024, the leading producers of tobacco (unmanufacture) in the world are – (1) China (2.26 million tonnes), (2) India (0.73 million tonnes), (3) Brazil (0.64 million tonnes), (4) Indonesia (0.53 million tonnes) and (5) Zimbabwe (0.24 million tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Rubber is obtained from the latex of a tree found in the equatorial evergreen forests. Rubber trees are tropical trees that require a temperature of 25° to 30° and an average annual rainfall of 150 to 200 cm. According to FAO 2024, the top 5 leading producers of natural rubber in the world are – 1. Thailand (4789.04 thousand tonnes), 2. Indonesia (2262.09 thousand tonnes), 3. Cote d'Ivoire (1686.59 thousand tonnes),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • 4. Vietnam (1327.47 thousand tonnes) and 5. China (877.60 thousand tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Coffee is a bush type of tree found in the tropical and subtropical regions. The Abyssinian Plateau (Ethiopia) is the native place of coffee. The main species of coffee are – (1) Coffea Arabica – It occupies 3/4 of the total coffee in the world. (2) Coffea Robusta – Grown on a large scale in Africa, in countries such as Ethiopia and Uganda. Robusta is grown in India.According to FAO 2024, the leading producers of green coffee in the world are – 1. Brazil (3387.72 thousand tonnes), 2. Vietnam (2015.29 thousand tonnes), 3. Colombia (839.85 thousand tonnes), 4. Indonesia (807.58 thousand tonnes), 5. Ethiopia (575.69 thousand tonnes), 6. Uganda (402.00 thousand tonnes), 7. India (363.00 thousand tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Tea is a plant of the tropical and subtropical regions but can also be grown in the hilly areas of the temperate zones. Tea requires a long summer with an average temperature between 20°-30°C. Tea also requires average rainfall between 130 and 150 cm.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to FAO 2024 China produces the maximum tea leaves (16260.90 thousand tonnes) in the world followed by India (6156.03 thousand tonnes), Kenya (2687.20 thousand tonnes), Sri Lanka (1514.02 thousand tonnes) and Turkiye (1414.00 thousand tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Tea was first used in China as a medicinal drink. Maize is the third most important grain after rice and wheat. It is native to Latin America. In Western cultures (mainly the U.S.A.), Maize is used as fodder for animals while in Latin America, it is consumed by people as food source. According to FAO 2024, the top 5 leading producer of Maize (corn) in world are – 1. USA (377632.69 thousand tonnes), 2. China (294920.00 thousand tonnes), 3. Brazil (114953.30 thousand tonnes), 4. Argentina (57494.50 thousand tonnes), 5. India (40230.57 thousand tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Plantation agriculture is mostly practiced in tropical regions. It is practiced on small pieces of land rather than in large estates. Every region has some specific crop growing in that place.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare plantation crops include Coconut, Cocoa, Arecanut and Chashew nuts. However according to Ministry of Commerce and Industry plantation crops include – Tea, Coffee, Rubber and Spices. Hence, plantation agriculture includes – Coconut, Arecanut, Cocoa, Cashew nut, Tea, Coffee, Rubber and Spices.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Horticulture includes Pomology (Cultivation of Fruits), Olericulture (cultivation of Vegetables) and Floriculture (Cultivation of Flowers). Now, Mushrooms, Bamboo, Spices etc. have also been brought under the definition of Horticulture. Horticulture requires a lot of manual labor. Coffee cultivation is a horticultural practice in Hawaii (USA). The coffee of Hawaii is famously known as Kona coffee. Mocha coffee is produced in Yemen. Mocha is the name of the harbor from where it is imported.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • The diverse climate of India ensures the production of a variety of vegetables and fruits. According to FAO, 2024 India is the largest producer of fruit (other fruit, n.e.c.), and second largest producer of vegetables (other vegetables, fresh n.e.c.) after China.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • In alley cropping, crops are grown in the spaces left between the trees planted in rows.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Taungya is a type of shifting agriculture practised in Myanmar. Chena, jhuming and milpa are also associated with shifting agriculture.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • The regions of Europe close to the Mediterranean Sea are famous for the cultivation of grapes. Around 85% of the total grapes produced are used for making wines.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Sacramento-San Joaquin Valley is located in California (USA). Sacramento is a flat/internal valley, the where River San Joaquin creates an inland delta. The valley is world famous for grapes and citrus fruit.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Golden Crescent is the name given to the countries that produce and export poppy. Countries included in the Golden Crescent are Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Groundnuts are native to Brazil, Mato Grosso and its nearby areas. Groundnut is the main crop of Gambia and has a major role to play in the country’s GDP (Gross Domestic Product). According to FAO, 2024 China is the largest producer of groundnuts excluding shelled in the world. Catechu (kattha) is obtained from the wood of Acacia catechu tree. First time in the world, American agronomist Norman Borlaug developed the high yielding variety (HYV) seeds in Mexico. According to the International Agreement on Agriculture, a Green Box is an instrument through which economic assistance is provided in the fields of– research related to control of insects and disease, training, general awareness, marketing and promotion activities.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Shahtoosh is a special woolen shawl made out of the hairs of Tibetan Antelope and Chiru. Chiru is found in the Chinese Autonomous Region of Tibet. Earlier it was also found in western Nepal. Chiru is also found in the union territory of Ladakh. Apiculture is associated with the rearing of honey bees for honey production.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Viticulture is associated with study and production of grapes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • According to FAO, 2023 China is the largest producer of raw silk in the world, followed by India. Other countries producing silk include Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Democratic People's Republic of Korea and Brazil.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Nitrogen is an essential element for the development of plants. It is important for the development of plant cells and tissues hence a deficiency of nitrogen hampers the growth of plants causing the leaves to turn yellowish in colour and dry up. Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum and blue-green algae are used as bio-fertilizers for crops.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Blue-green algae is used as a bio-fertilizer in paddy fields, whereas azotobacter is used as a bio-fertilizer for paddy wheat, maize, mustard, potato, cotton etc. Azospirillum is used as a bio-fertilizer for Paddy, Sorghum, Millet, Sugarcane, Maize etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Alfa-Alfa is a flowering plant of the Fabaceae pea family. It is cultivated as an important fodder crop. In the United Kingdom, Australia, South Africa and New Zealand, it is called Lucerne grass.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • Animal husbandry is more developed in those regions where natural grazing lands or grasslands are found in abundance. The credit for commercializing animal husbandry is given to European migrants. Ranches are large farms for cattle grazing. They are built by enclosing natural grasslands with barbed wire and then using them as grazing lands for livestock. Maximum livestocks is found in Asia. According to FAO 2020, the countries with maximum livestock population are – China (829.58 million), India (545.33 million), Brazil (304.15 million), and USA (201.69 million). Western Europe, USA, Canada, Russia, Australia and New Zealand are important regions of dairy farming. According to the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics, 2025 milk production in the country (India) continues to increase as it is anticipated to be 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25 with a per capita availability of milk at about 485 grams/day. According to World Food and Agriculture Statistical Yearbook, 2025 the top five leading producers (2023) of milk (bovine milk) in the world are – India (231.49 million tonnes), USA (102.68 million tonnes), Pakistan (62.54 million tonnes), China (45.71 million tonnes), and Brazil (36.44 million tonnes).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Which one of the following is not a type of shifting cultivation?Fazenda

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Minerals: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          (i) Coal

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • When small pieces of rock collect below the surface, it leads to the formation of sedimentary rock also known as layered rocks. Fossils and fossil fuels are found in the sedimentary rocks. Sedimentary rocks occupy 75% of the total Earth's surface.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Minerals such as coal, slate, marble, salt (rock), petroleum are found in sedimentary rocks. Coal and limestone are examples of sedimentary rocks ofbiotic origin.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Based on the percentage of carbon present coal is categorized into four types–(1) Anthracite - It is the best quality of coal having a carbon content of 90%–95%. (2) Bituminous – It is next to Anthracite in terms of quality having a carbon content of 70% to 90%. (3) Lignite - Famously known as brown coal having a carbon content of 45%–50%. It is mostly used in thermal power plants. (4) Peat –It is low-grade coal having a carbon content of 40% or less. Rock coal is also known as Anthracite. It is the highest quality of coal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to data from World Mineral Production 2019-2023 in the year 2023, China produced more than half of the world's production of coal. The top three leading producers (2022) of coal in the world are – (1) China, (2) India, (3) Indonesia. The top 5 countries in terms reserves of coal in the world by the end of year 2023 are USA, Russia, China, Australia and India respectively.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The North Appalachian coal area is the largest coal area in the USA. The region produces the best quality of coal. The other important coal regions of USA are – South Appalachian, Western Interior coal region and the coal region of Rocky Mountains etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Ruhr is a river that flows through Germany. The Ruhr Valley is the main coal region and industrial area known as Ruhr Basin.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Saarland is located on the borders of France and Germany in the Saar River valley. This area is said to have huge deposits of coal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Donets Basin, also known as Donbass is currently located in Ukraine. It is an important coal producing region.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Provinces of Shaanxi and Sichuan in China are important coal producing areas. Kuznets Basin of Russia and Lancashire in the U.K. are also famous for coal production.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Minerals · The Iron Ore: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The most abundant metal found in Earth's core is iron. It is found along with Aluminium, Lime, Magnesia, Soapstone, Titanium, Arsenic, Copper, Phosphorus and other minerals. With the Industrial Revolution picking up pace the extraction of Iron also gained momentum.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23, the top five leading producers of iron ore in the world (in the year 2023) are –1. Australia (952.51 million metric tonnes), 2. Brazil (436.84 million metric tonnes), 3. India (277.96 million metric tonnes), 4. China (250.00 million metric tonnes), 5. Russia (90.80 million metric tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, 2026 top five leading countries in the world in terms of iron content reserves are–(1) Australia (2) Brazil (3) Russia (4) Mauritania (5) India.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Krivoy Rog region of Ukraine and Magnitogorsk in Russia are famous for iron ore production.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The Pilbara region and Hamersley mine area of Australia are famous for iron ore extraction.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In USA large scale production of iron ore is done in Minnesota and Michigan.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Minerals · The Copper: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Copper is the most important metal after Iron in the field of industries.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Huge reserves of copper are found on the western slope of Andes Mountains, ranging from northern Peru to central Chile.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to World Mineral Production 2019- 23 in the year 2023 Chile is the largest producer of copper ore.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Huge deposits of porphyry copper are found in the mountainous region of Andes. The Chuquicamata copper mine in northern Chile is located in this region. These copper deposits are believed to be of post Eocene, Oligocene epoch. Copper was first produced in the USA in the Keweenaw Peninsula of the state of Michigan. Apart from this copper was also produced in the Butte region of Montana in the USA.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • The largest copper producing area of Canada is Sudbury (Ontario). Also, the Canadian regions of Flin Flon and Britannia Beach are famous for copper production. Katanga province of Democratic Republic of the Congo is known for copper mining. It is located near the border of Zambia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Zambia is a landlocked country in Africa. There is a long copper (reserve) belt from Zambia to Katanga (D. R. Congo). Though this belt has large deposits of copper, the lack of marine transport dilutes the possibilities of trading and export of the region's copper.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Japan is self-sufficient in copper production. The production of copper in Japan is more than its consumption.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The top Five leading countries in terms of copper reserves are – Chile, Australia, Peru, Russia/Congo, and Mexico.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to the figures of World Mineral Production 2019- 23 the top five leading countries in terms of copper production (in 2023) are–(1) Chile, (2) Democratic Republic of the Congo (3) Peru (4) China and (5) USA.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Minerals · The Gold: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Gold is obtained from two sources. In natural form, it is are found in the layers of quartz rocks as rock gold it is also found as small granules in placer deposits of rivers.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to the figures of Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2024, Australia has the largest gold reserve. The province boasts of two of the world famous gold mines–the Coolgardie and Kalgoorlie. Gold is being extracted from Mount Morgan in Australia. The important gold deposits of USA are found in South Dakota, Black Hills,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Salt Lake, Alaska and the Yuba region of California.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In Canada, gold is being extracted from the provinces of Quebec and Ontario.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Important gold producing areas of China are Yunnan, Manchuria and Tsingling Shan.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Important gold producing areas of South Africa are Johannesburg, Mponeng, Boxberg, etc. It is famous for the extraction of gold and diamonds.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23 the largest producers of gold (In 2023) are–(1) China, (2) Russia, (3) Australia, (4) Canada.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, 2026 the top three leading countries in the world in terms of gold reserves are–Australia, Russia and South Africa.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Minerals · The Silver: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Silver is the second most precious metal after gold and is used for making ornaments, coins, electroplating, photography and medicinal purposes. It is found in free elemental form in nature in metamorphic rocks, 2026.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to figures from the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, 2026. The top four countries with the largest silver reserves are–Peru (110000 tonnes), Russia (92,000 tonnes), Australia (91000 tonnes), China (67000 tonnes), Poland (59000 tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23. The top five countries in terms of silver (metal content) production (2023) are– Mexico, China, Peru, Poland and Russia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • German silver is also known as, nickel silver, paktong, new silver, alpacca, etc. It is an alloy comprised of 60% copper, 20% zinc and 20% nickel (However according to NCERT the composition of German silver is Cu (25-30%), Zn (25-30%) and Ni (40-50%). Hence, the alloy does not contain any silver. Since it shines like silver it was given the name German silver.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Minerals · The Aluminium: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Aluminium is a whitish colored metal. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          According to World Mineral Production 2019-23, in the year 2023, the top five leading countries in terms of aluminium (primary) production were–China, Russia, India, Canada and UAE. The Cape York Peninsula and Weipa region of Australia, the Saline County of Arkansas (USA), the Cola Peninsula of the Russia are some important regions of the world where Bauxite production is being done.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Minerals · The Tin: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • About 80% of the world's tin is found in placer deposits. These deposits are located in riverbeds and Valleys or on the sea floor. Maximum placer deposits are spread across South East Asia. Most of the tin deposits in China are found in the plateau region of Yunnan.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • In Indonesia tin is produced from the Sumatra islands of Bangka and Belitung. In Malaysia, tin is produced from the Kinta Valley (Perak province), Kuala Lumpur, and Pahang province. In South America, tin deposits are found in the eastern Andes region, within a belt.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23 as per the figures of the year 2023, the top five leading producers of tin (mine production) in the world are – China (66500 tonnes), Indonesia (50669 tonnes), Myanmar (47081 tonnes), Peru (26230 tonnes) and Brazil (25121 tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • Coal is an example of –Sedimentary

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Coal → sedimentary rock (layered; holds fossils and mineral oil). Coal grades: anthracite (90-95% carbon) > bituminous (most abundant) > lignite (brown coal) > peat.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Minerals · The Petroleum: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Petroleum is a liquid, formed as a result of different mixtures ofhydrocarbons. Petroleum is a multicolored substance. The multicolours are due to the mixture of different chemicals present in it. Petroleum is found in sedimentary rocks. It gets accumulates in the stoma and interstices of porous sandstones and limestones.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The first commercial oil well was drilled in Romania in 1857. Romania is the first country in the world whose crude oil production has an official document (1857 AD. 275 tonnes) and was recorded at the international level. However according to the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, GOI Edwin L. Drake drilled the worlds first oil well in 1859 at Titusville, Pennsylvania, U.S.A. According to Indian Minerals Year Book 2022, the largest share of reserves of world crude oil is available in Middle East (48.3%), followed by South & Central America (18.7%), North America (14%), CIS (8.4%), Africa (7.2%), Asia Pacific (2.6%) and Europe (0.8%).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • According to World Population Review data in 2024, the top three leading countries in terms of crude oil proved reserves are – Venezuela (303.2 Billion Barrels), Saudi Arabia (267.2 Billion Barrels) and Iran (208.6 Billion Barrels).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23 (data 2023) the largest crude oil producers in the world are – USA (874.11 million tonnes), Russia (541.70 million tonnes), Saudi Arabia (531.70 million tonnes), Canada (277.90 million tonnes), Iran (214.30 million tonnes).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The important petroleum producing countries in Asia are – Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar etc.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The largest oil-producing country in South-East Asia is Indonesia. Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan are the important oil producing regions of Indonesia. In China oil is produced in Sichuan, Shanxi, Yumen and Saidum which lie in the North-Western part. Crude oil is produced in 32 U.S. states and in U.S. coastal waters.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • In Canada petroleum is produced in Alberta province (Leduc region), Manitoba and British Columbia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • In the former Soviet Union petroleum was produced in the Volga-Ural region, Baku region (Azerbaijan) and regions lying in proximity the Caspian Sea. The country of Venezuela in South America is an important oil-producing country in the world. Petroleum exports constitute more than 80% (2025) of the total exports of Venezuela. Large scale production of petroleum is done in Brazil and Colombia. Normally mineral oil is found in those places where other fossil fuels are found. It is also found independently in some places.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • According to the data of Statistical Review of World Energy 2025, the top five leading countries in terms of natural gas reserves are – (1) Russia (2) Iran, (3) Qatar (4) USA and (5) Saudi Arabia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The top five leading producers of natural gas in the world (2023) are – (1) USA (2) Russia, (3) Iran, (4) China (5) Qatar.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Gasohol is usually 90% Gasoline (unleaded) and usually 10% ethyl alcohol (ethanol) whereas gasoline or petrol is a mixture derived from petroleum. Hence, the largest producer and consumer of gasohol will be the one who produces a large amount of gasoline and ethanol. USA is the largest producer of Ethanol also in 2025. Hence, at present, USA is the largest producer and consumer of gasohol.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Brent crude oil is one of the classifications of crude oil and also the largest one. It comprises Brent Crude, Brent Sweet, Light crude, Oseberg Ekofisk and Fortis (BFOE). Brent Crude is extracted from the North Sea. It has a sulphur content of 0.37%. Brent crude is used in the 2/3rd of the world's internationally trade crude oil supplies.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Sugarcane, Maize, Soyabean, Rapeseed and Jatropha is used for producing Bio fuels. The alcohol produced by sugarcane and Maize can be mixed with petroleum to produce Gasohol. Thus, reducing the problem of fossil fuel pollution. The oil extracted from Jatropha can be mixed with diesel to produce Biodiesel, which could be used as an alternative to diesel.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Gas pipeline between Iran and Pakistan has been given the name Peace Pipeline.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Minerals · The Uranium: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Uranium was discovered in 1789 by Martin Klaproth. It is extracted from an ore named Pitchblende. Uranium and Thorium are two important sources of atomic power.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • According to the figures of World Mineral Production Data 2019-23, in the year 2023, Kazakhstan is the leading producer of Uranium in the world followed by Canada, Namibia, Australia and Uzbekistan. India is the 9th largest country in Uranium production).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Australia has the largest uranium reserve in the world.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Cigar Lake mine of Canada is the mine with the largest production of Uranium situated in a single place. Olympic Dam mine situated in Australia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Uranium is extracted from the Sinkolobwe mine located in Katanga region in the country of Democratic Republic of the Congo. Uranium City is located in Canada. It is located on the Northern shores of Lake Athabasca.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Other important reserves of Uranium in the world are Port Radium and Elliot Lake of Canada, Colorado Plateau of USA, Radium Hill and Marry Katheline of Australia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • Radium is a radioactive chemical element. It is extracted from the ore of Uranium, which is Pitchblende.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The maximum known quantity of Thorium has been found in the coastal beach sand of Kerala (India) and from the eastern coast of Brazil, especially from the Espirito Santo region. Thorium is also found in the southeastern and Western mountains regions of USA, Nigeria, South Africa Union, Russian Federation and Indonesia (Sumatra).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Mineral: Miscellaneous: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • The Bauxite reserves of the world are estimated to be around
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • 29.00 million tonnes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • According to the figures of USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, 2026, the leading countries in terms of bauxite reserves are – (1) Guinea, (2) Australia,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • (3) Vietnam, (4) Indonesia and (5) Jamaica. According to World Mineral Production 2019-23 (Data-2023), Guinea is the top producer of Bauxite in the world, accounting for almost 29.56% of the total global production. Guinea is followed by Australia and China respectively. In this above context, India ranks 6th.

The largest producer of tin is China, followed by Indonesia, Myanmar, and Peru.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • – (1) Russia (37316754 carats), (2) Botswana (25095000 carats), (3) Canada (16160688 carats), (4) Angola (9754310 carats) and (5) D.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 • On global scale China ranks first in the production of rare earth metals, accounting about 70% of the total global production. The production of these metals is not only complex but also harmful to the environment. Since the metals can easily be imported from, China hence a lot of countries have stopped production in their own lands. After years of exploitation of this resource, finally, in 2010, China declared to cut back on the production as well as the export of the rare soil metals.

(2) Bheemseni kapur is found occurring in natural form in Sumatra and Borneo. It is extracted from the Dryobalanops Aromatica tree which belongs to Dipterocarpaceae family. (3) Patri Kapoor is extracted in India. It is extracted from the plants belonging to Blumea species of Compositae family.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • A footloose industry is an industry which can be placed and located at any place and is independent of factors such as transport. The best example of the footloose industries is diamond and computer chip industries. Since the electronics industry is not heavily dependent on raw materials, it is hence considered a footloose industry.
