                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The Transport: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The highways are better developed and proliferated in developed countries as compared to developing countries.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Trans Canadian Highway connects the city of Saint Johns (Newfoundland and Labrador) located in the eastern coast of Canada to Vancouver city in British Columbia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Alaska Highway begins in Dawson Creek, British Columbia and runs to Delta Junction, Alaska.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Pan American Highway connects South America, Middle Americas to USA and Canada. Stuart Highway connects Darwin in the Northern Territory of Australia, to Melbourne in Victoria via Alice spring to Port Augusta in South Australia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • China is a large country whose important cities are connected via road networks. The main highway of Russia connects its capital Moscow to Irkutsk city of the Siberian region.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Capital of Egypt, Cairo is connected to Cape Town in South Africa through an intercontinental highway (Trans-African Highway-4).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Commercial air transport was started by USA in the year 1914, which later proliferated to different parts of the world.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • There is a dense network of air routes in Western Europe, Eastern USA and southeast Asia. Major air routes are centred in some important places. Among these, some important locations are London, Paris, Rome, Moscow, Karachi, Delhi, Mumbai, Bangkok, Singapore, Tokyo, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Chicago, New York, Rio-de-Janeiro, Karachi, Delhi, Mumbai, etc. The air routes of these places have been arranged according to their respective distances for example, the international flight from Delhi to Tokyo travels on an international route having stoppages at the airports of Bangkok (Thailand), Hanoi (Vietnam), Hong Kong (China) and Taipei City (Taiwan) respectively.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Some long-distance air routes of the world are:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (1) Newyork–London–Paris–Rome–Cairo–Delhi–Kolkata– Hongkong–Tokyo route.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (2) New York–San Francisco–Honolulu–Hong Kong– Adelaide–Perth route.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The important passenger airlines of USA are–American Airlines, Delta Airlines and Southwest Airlines.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • All Nippon Airways is most important passenger airline in Japan. Air China is China’s air service.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Lufthansa is Germany’s passenger airline service.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Emirates is passenger airline service of United Arab Emirates.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The world first public rail transport took place in 1825 between Stockton in Northern England and Darlington.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • According to World Bank data in terms of total Rail lines in km (in 2021), the top 5 countries are - USA > China > Russia > India > Canada. United States of America (according to data from the year 2021) has railway lines (total rail lines km) of 14,8553 km. similarily, 109767 km in China, 85544 km in Russia and 68103 km in India.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The world’s longest railway route is Trans-Siberian Railway (about 9300 km.). Starting from West of Eurasia in Leningrad, it connects the city of St. Petersburg to Vladivostok which is located in the eastern coast of Pacific Ocean. Note- The main track of Trans-Siberian Railway extends from Vladivostok to Moscow. By using a connecting service it can be traveled to Saint Petersburg in west.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Trans Andes is the most important rail route of South America. It connects Valparaiso in Chile to Buenos Aires in Argentina.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Orient Express is the most important rail route of Europe. It passes through 8 major countries of Europe. Orient Express connects LC Haure and Paris to the capital of Turkiye i.e. Istanbul. This train operated until 2009.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The Trans-European Railway connects the capital of France Paris to Warsaw (Poland).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • The construction of Canadian Pacific Railway completed in the year 1885.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Trans–Australian Railway. It connects originally Port Augusta in South Australia to Kalgoorlie in Western Australia. If latter expanded from Sydney in New South Wales to Perth in Western Australia.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Water transport is a relatively inexpensive mode of transport. The important oceanic trade routes of the world are–(1) North Atlantic Ocean route connects the North American industrial region to the industrial regions of Europe. (2) The Mediterranean sea and Indian Ocean route connects the developed regions of Western Europe to developing regions of East Africa, South Asia and East Asia, Via Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. (3) Suez Canal Route connects the Mediterranean Sea to Red sea. Among all the European countries, Britain has benefited the most from the Suez Canal Route. (4) Cape of Hope route - Prior to the opening of Suez Canal it was the only waterwat option of available. The route made the ships all along the African continent to reach the Red Sea. (5) South Atlantic Route connects the countries of Western Europe and Western Africa to Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay of South America. Some other important sea routes include – North Pacific route, South Pacific route and Panama Canal.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Delaware Aqueduct is located in USA. It is the largest rock tunnel in the world. The tunnel is 137 km. long and 13.5 feet to 19.5 feet broad and is used to carry New York city’s water supply. It has been constructed by drilling the hard rocks.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Paijanne water tunnel of Finland is 120 km. long and is the second longest tunnel used for carrying water supply.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Bolmen water tunnel of Sweden is 82 km. long and is used to carry water supply. The Channel Tunnel connects the U.K. and France; it is operated by Eurotunnel.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The Ports and Harbours: key facts from the book

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Sea routes are the most convenient and prevalent medium for any country to conduct its International trade. The ports and harbours of any country is well connected via railway networks and inland waterways. These connections provide the hinterland accessibility to the ports and harbours.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • According to World Shipping Council, in 2024 the top five leading harbours in the world based on their container capacity are as follows–(1) Shanghai (China), (2) Singapore,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • (3) Ningbo - Zhoushan (China), (4) Shenzhen (China), (5) Qingdao (China).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Singapore, Rotterdam, Copenhagen are important ports of the world.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Port of call are those ports where ships make a stoppage for refuelling, taking basic amenities like food and water for their travelers etc. before traveling further. Aden is the best example of port of call.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Maracaibo (Venezuela), Skhira (Tunisia), Tripoli (Libya) and Kolkata (India) are some of the important ports of the world, where facilities are available for emptying and refuelling of oil tankers.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Maracaibo port is located in Venezuela near Maracaibo Lake. It is connected to the sea through a 55 km. long strait. Maracaibo Lake has abundant resources of fossil fuels.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Santos is a harbour located in Brazil. At present it is the largest exporter of coffee in the world due to which it is also known as the Coffee Port.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Port Nolloth of South Africa is also known as Diamond Port.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Port Nolloth was constructed with its commercial importance in mind since it lies in the proximity of the diamond producing regions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Gwadar is a port in Pakistan located the Arabian Sea. The port has tactical importance in the region. An agreement was signed between Pakistan and China for the development of Gwadar Port. China is also building a rail network up to the Gwadar Port for the smooth transit of trade activities.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Tokyo is the capital of Japan and is a port city located on the Island of Honshu.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • New York is a port city located in USA. The city is located on the banks of the river Hudson.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Other important harbours of the world are Igarka (Russia), Montevideo (Uruguay) and Jakarta (Indonesia).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Alexandria is the most important port city of Egypt. It is located in the deltaic region of the river Nile and is famous for the export of cotton textiles.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Rotterdam Harbour is in the Netherlands and is located on the Nieuwe Mass, a distributary in the Rhine - Meuse delta.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • London is a port city located on the river Thames.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Yokohama is an important harbour in Japan.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The Mapping: key facts from the book
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Maps provide us with relevant information regarding regional, territorial and local changes.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Isopleth maps provide us information about regions or areas having continuous distribution. Thus isopleths are lines joining places of equal value of quantity, intensity, equal pressure, equal temperature, equal rainfall, equal salinity etc. A very relevant and precise data is required for drawing the lines of isopleths. If there is equitable distribution of the given subject then isopleths become very useful. Moreover, the use of isopleths becomes difficult if the subject is in constant fluctuation for exp. population density.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Contours represent elevation topography in comparison to the sea level. It is the most practical and widely used method in showing elevations on a map. When the contours of Isotypes are drawn very close to each other then it signifies steep slopes. Isohypse - isohypse or height contour is a line of equal geopotential height, which are shown on a constant pressure surface. Isogonic lines show the earth’s magnetic declination on a map. Isobaths are imaginary lines, a map that links points at the same depth below the water surface.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Isobars are imaginary lines drawn on the maps that links areas having equal air pressure at mean sea level.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Isohyets are lines on the map joining areas having an equal amount of rainfall.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Isonifs are lines on the mapjoining areas having an equal amount of snowfall.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Isohalines are lines on the map joining areas having an equal amount of salinity.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following country is not a member of the OPEC:China

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Not an OPEC member → China; Algeria and UAE are members; Indonesia suspended membership in January 2009 (finally 30 November 2016).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The headquarter of SAARC is:Kathmandu

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            SAARC Secretariat → Kathmandu, Nepal; eight South Asian members; idea first raised by Bangladesh President Ziaur Rahman (2 May 1980); first summit in Dhaka.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Consider the following countries:2 and 5

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Organization of Turkic States (2009): founders Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkiye; Uzbekistan joined (October 2019). From the list → Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Where is ‘The leaning tower of Pisa’ located?Italy

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Leaning Tower of Pisa → Pisa, Italy; a free-standing bell tower (campanile) in Pisa's Cathedral Square.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Where is the Elysee Palace?France

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Elysee Palace → Paris, France; official residence of the French President since 1848.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which is the tallest among flyer birds?Crane

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Tallest flying bird → crane; ostrich is the tallest bird but cannot fly.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which country has the largest number of Post Offices?India

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Largest number of post offices → India (164999 as on March 31, 2025).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The Chernobyl nuclear disaster occurred in:Ukraine

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Chernobyl nuclear disaster → April 1986, Ukraine (then part of the Soviet Union).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Due to ' The Great Leap Forward Policy' million people had to die of starvation in:China

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            'Great Leap Forward' (1958-1962, second five-year plan) → China; millions died of starvation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Arrange the following countries in the descending order of their number of nuclear power plants and select the correct answer from the codes given below: 1 France 3 Japan 2 Russia 4 U. S. A. Code:4, 1, 2, 3

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Nuclear power plants, descending, when asked: USA > France > Russia > Japan; IAEA (March 31, 2026): USA, France, China, Russia, Republic of Korea.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the countries in descending order of their nuclear power capacity as per 2012?France, Japan, Russia, China

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Nuclear power capacity, descending (2012, among options): France, Japan, Russia, China; IAEA 2026: USA, France, China, Russia.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In which of the following countries 99 percent of its total energy requirement is obtained by Hydro-Power?Norway

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            About 99 percent of energy needs from hydropower → Norway; China ranks first in installed hydro capacity (2024).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The name of which of the following countries closely means "country of 40 tribes"?Kyrgyzstan

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            'Country of 40 tribes' → Kyrgyzstan ('Kyrk' = forty); epic 'Manas' tells of hero Manas who united the 40 tribes.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which pair amongst the following is not correctly matched?The queen of Adriatic sea - Rome

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Wrong pair: Queen of the Adriatic – Rome; it is Venice. Correct: Lorraine coal fields – France; West Midlands – Birmingham; Tula – Russia.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The Peneplain is related to:river

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Peneplain → made by rivers: almost featureless, gently undulating plain worn nearly to base level; term coined by (William) Morris Davis.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • What is meant by the term 'Umland'?Area surrounding a town

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Umland → region surrounding a city, linked to it by inflow and outflow relations.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Among the following whose name is associated with migration theory?Lee

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Migration theory → Everett Lee; he saw migration as a permanent or semi-permanent change of residence.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Indian Ocean hosts military bases of big powers (A true) as it offers strong geo-political benefits (R true); UPPSC key: R not the correct explanation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Which of the following statement is not true?Species diversity increases from equator towards poles.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Not true: species diversity rises from equator to poles; it falls from equator towards poles. Tropics have more species; Amazon rainforest has greatest biodiversity.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The word 'Denisovan' is sometimes mentioned in media in reference toan early human species

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Denisovan → early human species; first found 2008 in Denisova cave, Altai mountains (Siberia); a jawbone shows them on the Tibetan Plateau 1,60,000 years ago.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • The line joining the areas having the same rainfall is calledIsohyet

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Isohyet → line joining places of equal rainfall; isobar → pressure; isotherm → temperature; isohaline → salinity.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Geostationary satellite revolves at:At fixed height

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Geostationary satellite → at a fixed height (about 35,786 km) over the equator, moving west to east with Earth's rotation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • Dalmatian Coast is:Foot-hills of Karst

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Dalmatian Coast (Croatia, Adriatic Sea) → foot-hills of karst; one of the world's most rugged coastlines, with karst topography.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • In which country was the world’s largest offshore wind farm inaugurated in August 2024?United Kingdom

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            World's largest operational offshore wind farm per the book → Hornsea 2, North Sea, United Kingdom (1.32 GW); UPPSC's answer is Taiwan.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Full question and explanation · 1 paper(s)
